[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Chapter 1. Turbonomic 8.16.0 Documentation]

Documentation for this product release includes the following general topics.

- Release Notes - Describes new features, improvements, deprecated/removed features, and known issues
- Installation - Helps you install Turbonomic in your on-prem environment
- Updating Turbonomic - Helps you perform a Turbonomic update
- SaaS Setup - Helps you set up a SaaS client in your on-prem environment, so that a SaaS server in the public cloud can manage your on-prem workloads
- Product Overview - Provides an overview of the platform and its underlying architecture
- Getting Started - Describes login steps, the Home Page, actions, and policies
- Target Configuration - Provides a list of targets that the product can monitor, and describes how to configure each target properly
- User Interface Reference - Provides a list entities discovered from targets, and describes how to configure plans, charts, and administrative settings
- API Reference - Helps you use the REST API as you script interactions with the product
- Integration - Data Ingestion Framework - Describes how to set up Data Ingestion Framework, a feature that enables you to define custom entities and entity metrics for your environment, and load them into the platform for analysis
- Integration - Data Exporter - Describes how to set up Data Exporter, a feature that streams Turbonomic data about entities and actions as JSON documents, and then publishes the data to a Kafka topic
- Integration - SaaS Reporting - Describes how to set up SaaS Reporting, a SaaS-based add-on that stores a history of your managed environment and presents this history via Liveboards and reports
- Integration - Embedded Reporting - Describes how to set up Embedded Reporting, an add-on that stores a history of your managed environment and presents this history via dashboards and reports

Turbonomic also integrates with ServiceNow, a third-party change management application. To view the documentation for this integration, see Turbonomic Actions for ServiceNow.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Chapter 2. Release notes]

Release Date: April 30, 2025

These release notes describe the following for Turbonomic 8.16.0:

- New features
- Feature updates and notices
- Improvements
- Known issues
- REST API changes

To update to version 8.16.0, your Turbonomic version must be at least 8.8.0. If you currently run an older version of Turbonomic, you must update to version 8.8.0 first. For assistance in updating to the minimum required version, contact your Turbonomic representative.

To view the release notes for earlier versions of the product, go to this page.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Application performance management]

- New underlying entity types for application maps : Starting with 8.15.3, you can create or update an application map that includes the following newly supported entity types and then view the corresponding supply chain:
- Application component spec
- Document collection
- Virtual machine spec

For more information, see Application map.

- Support for .NET applications : Turbonomic can now discover and collect metrics from .NET applications on Datadog, Dynatrace, Instana and New Relic targets.
- Simplified database password configuration for Oracle targets : You can now update Oracle database passwords in bulk by uploading a CSV file through the Turbonomic user interface. This feature enables IT Ops teams to regularly rotate their passwords for multiple Oracle targets without having to manually update each target. For more information, see Updating Oracle database passwords in bulk.
- Removal of support for JBoss targets : As of version 8.15.1, Turbonomic no longer supports JBoss targets. After you upgrade to version 8.15.1 or later, delete any existing JBoss targets from the Target Configuration page by selecting the target and clicking Delete . Also, it is recommended that you delete jboss and mediation-jboss related settings from the Turbonomic Custom Resource (CR) file. For more information, see (Optional) Enabling and disabling probe components.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Container platform resource management]

- Target configuration wizard for container platform targets : When you add a Kubernetes or Red Hat OpenShift target in the Target Configuration page, you will now see a Connect Target option that launches a target configuration wizard. This wizard streamlines the target deployment process by prompting for the required settings and generating a script. You can then download the script and run it in your Kubernetes or Red Hat OpenShift cluster to complete the deployment. For more information, see Deploying to a Kubernetes cluster and Deploying to a Red Hat OpenShift cluster.
- Automation of scale actions for workloads managed by Knative Serving : Turbonomic can now automate scale actions for workloads managed by Knative Serving. Turbonomic automatically detects and updates the minimum and maximum replicas to the values configured in the Knative Service Custom Resource (CR). The Knative Serving controller then scales the workloads accordingly.

No additional setup is required to enable Knative Serving support in Turbonomic.

For more information, see Support for Knative Serving.

- Multi-instance GPU (MIG) aware horizontal scale actions for Kubernetes GenAI LLM workloads : If your NVIDIA GPUs are partitioned using MIG, Turbonomic now recognizes the GPU partitions and recommends MIG-aware horizontal scale actions for Kubernetes GenAI LLM workloads accordingly. To generate scale actions, Turbonomic analyzes GPU metrics that Prometurbo collects from a customermanaged Prometheus instance. For more information, see MIG-aware horizontal scale actions.
- New performance metric for container platform services that back AI workloads : For workloads running large language models in Kubernetes, Turbonomic now leverages a vLLM metric called percentage of KV cache usage ( vllm:gpu\_cache\_usage\_perc ). The Prometurbo agent for Turbonomic collects this metric from Prometheus and then continuously monitors it as a performance metric for container platform services. When you set Service Level Objectives (SLOs) in policies for these container platform services, Turbonomic can generate SLO-driven scale actions to prevent resource bottlenecks and maximize the performance of AI workloads, while keeping cache usage within the desired thresholds. For more information, see Container platform service policies.
- Automated execution of resize up actions for container vCPU and vMem requests : Automated action execution is now supported for resize up actions for container vCPU and vMem requests. Previously, these actions were only manually executable in the Turbonomic user interface or directly in your container platform cluster. For more information, see Resizing resource limits and requests.
- Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization target configuration : Turbonomic now discovers Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization resources through a new or existing target configuration with Red Hat OpenShift. For more information, see Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization.
- Go-based operator for Prometurbo : Prometurbo now uses a Go-based operator to enable automatic changes to the Prometurbo deployment. With this improvement, you no longer need to update or delete resources manually.

For Prometurbo deployments in Red Hat OpenShift OperatorHub, the new Go-based operator is available as the certified edition in Prometurbo's stable channel. Prometurbo automatically switches from the Helm-based operator to the Go-based operator if your approval strategy is Automatic. If your approval strategy is Manual, OperatorHub notifies you that an operator update is available. Approve the update when you see the notification.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > On-prem resource management]

- Hot add for vMEM and vCPU : This release introduces new Enable vCPU hot add and Enable vMEM hot add settings for vCenter VMs in the on-prem VM policy settings. When these settings are enabled, Turbonomic can resize vCPU or vMEM for vCenter VMs without restarting the scoped VMs. You can enable hot add only for vCenter VMs that meet the following conditions:
- Fault tolerance is not enabled.
- VMware tools is installed.
- Virtual hardware version is 11 or later.

The hot add feature is provided by vCenter and might be subject to other vendor limitations. For more information, see On-prem VM policies and the vCenter documentation.

- Support for forcing minimum sizing for on-prem virtual machines : Turbonomic now supports configuring policies to take resize actions when virtual machines (VMs) are out of compliance. With this feature, you can bring the vCPU and vMem parameters of a VM into compliance by running the recommended compliance actions that are generated based on VM policies. You can also update policy settings to prevent compliance actions from being generated for specific VMs. With the availability of this feature, the listed generated resize actions for your VMs can now include compliance actions. For more information about this feature or updating your policy settings for generating compliance actions, see Forced minimum sizing for on-prem VMs.
- Resize of on-premises VMs even when they are powered off : A new Resize when powered off setting in the on-premises VM automation policies enables Turbonomic to resize VMs even when they are powered off. This setting is useful in environments where powered-off VMs must be resized according to the anticipated load when they are restarted. This feature is available in vSphere, VMM, and Hyper-V environments. For more information, see On-prem VM policies.
- Dynamic filter on VM reservation : Placement policies for initial placement can include VM dynamic filter restrictions when the backend feature flag is enabled. A VM reservation will be processed only if the selected VM template's attributes (CPUs, memory size, and storage) match the dynamic filters in the placement policy groups. This applies only to dynamic filters with any of these three attributes.
- Support for plans with IBM PowerVM environments : For an IBM PowerVM environment, you can now configure and use Optimize on-prem and Hardware refresh plans. Other plans are not currently supported for IBM PowerVM environments.
- Grace period for delete actions : This release introduces a change to storage policies to avoid unintentional manual deletion of unattached files when the actions are in Manual mode. Any Delete Unattached Files actions that are generated in the grace period between the Generate Delete Action after <your configured number of> Days and the Delete file after <your configured number of> Days settings are created in Recommend mode only, and cannot be executed. After this grace period expires, the action can be executed according to the configured settings. For more information, see Storage settings.
- Removal of support for VMware Horizon targets : As of version 8.15.5, Turbonomic no longer supports VMware Horizon targets. After you upgrade to version 8.15.5 or later, delete any existing Horizon targets from the Target Configuration page by selecting the target and clicking Delete . Also, it is recommended that you delete horizon and mediation-horizon related settings from the Turbonomic Custom Resource (CR) file. For more information, see (Optional) Enabling and disabling probe components.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Cloud resource management]

- Disruptiveness and reversibility information for cloud VM scale actions : All scale actions for cloud VMs are disruptive but reversible. These actions require downtime but VMs can be scaled back to their previous tiers or sizes if needed. Scale actions in Action Center now show this information to help you decide whether to execute actions immediately or defer execution to a later time.
- Support for AWS io2 volumes attached to Relational Database Service (RDS) : Turbonomic now discovers io2 volumes that are attached to RDS instances and recommends scaling these volumes to optimize performance and cost.
- AWS Enterprise Discount Program (EDP) support for VM actions : Turbonomic now factors in EDP discounts when calculating savings associated with AWS VM actions. For more information, see AWS Billing target and scale actions.

To take advantage of this feature, you need to set up an AWS standard data export (CUR 2.0). If a standard data export is already set up, the following configurations are required:

- Add line\_item\_net\_unblended\_cost to the standard data export. For more information, see Setting up a standard data export (CUR 2.0).
- Configure EDP discounts in the Price adjustment tab of the Billing and costs page. For more information, see Price adjustment.

- Guidelines for AWS environments with service control policies (SCPs) : Turbonomic connects to various AWS services and endpoints to discover workloads and pricing data. To successfully connect to these services and endpoints, Turbonomic must not be blocked by SCPs. The documentation now provides guidelines to help you verify the connection and update your SCPs if the connection fails. For more information, see Reviewing your AWS service control policies.
- Historically informed action generation for Azure workloads : Turbonomic now supports historically informed action generation for the following Azure workloads in both global Azure and Azure Government accounts:
- App service plans
- Cosmos DB containers
- Cosmos DB databases

Actions are informed by 14 days of historical utilization data and are generated as soon as a new Azure service principal target is added. To take advantage of this feature, add at least one Azure service principal target. For more information, see Historically informed action generation for Azure workloads.

- Support for net throughput metrics for Azure VMs : Turbonomic now discovers net throughput metrics for Azure VMs and takes these metrics into consideration when it recommends scale actions for the VMs. For more information, see Net throughput-aware scaling for Azure VMs.
- Discovery of Google Cloud managed instance groups (MIGs) : Turbonomic now discovers Google Cloud MIGs and presents them as Virtual Machine Spec entities in the supply chain. Use the Entity Information chart to view information for individual MIGs. For more information, see Virtual machine spec - Google Cloud managed instance group.

To take advantage of this feature, add the following permissions to the Google Cloud custom role that is assigned to the service account for Turbonomic.

- -compute.autoscalers.list
- -compute.instanceTemplates.list

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > User interface management]

- Migration of pages to the new design for the user interface : The following pages are now migrated to the new design for the user interface:
- Home
- Schedule
- Policies (placement, automation, and parking policies)

These policy types are now displayed as individual tabs in the Policies page so you can manage them with ease.

- Action center (including the Action details slideover window)

For more information, see New design for the user interface.

- Onboarding page in the UI for first time users : First time users are now shown an onboarding page in the UI when they first log in. This new page helps guide users through the initial required and recommended tasks for getting started with Turbonomic. For more information about this page and the getting started experience for first time users, see Getting started.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Reports]

- Support for SaaS Reporting in on-prem environments : Starting with version 8.15.4, the SaaS Reporting feature is available for on-prem Turbonomic installations. Previously, this feature was available only for SaaS instances. To begin the enablement process, verify that your company has an active IBM Passport Advantage agreement and then open a case with IBM support. Submit the case with a severity of 2 and provide the following details in the case description:
- The full name of your company
- The name and email address of your company's Turbonomic administrator
- Your Turbonomic instance ID. To obtain this value, SSH into your instance and run the following command:

```
kubectl exec consul[TAB] -- consul kv get instanceID
```

Your Turbonomic representative will begin processing enablement requests on March 31, 2025. Version 8.15.4 is now the minimum version for SaaS Reporting in all environment types. For more information, see Enabling SaaS reporting for on-prem instances.

- SaaS Reporting button enabled by default : Starting with 8.15.6, SaaS Reporting is enabled by default for all Turbonomic users. For on-premises deployments, an information icon appears next to the REPORTS (NEW) button. When users hover over the button, a one-time pop-up provides instructions on how to request provisioning of a SaaS reporting environment. This change is intended to improve user awareness and encourage adoption of the new reporting experience.
- New sustainability default Reporting Liveboard "Carbon Footprint - Public Cloud" : The new default Reporting Liveboard provides visibility into energy consumption and carbon emissions from public cloud VMs (AWS, Azure and Google Cloud). This Liveboard helps users track their environmental impact while uncovering opportunities to reduce energy usage and optimize workloads efficiently. For more information, see Carbon Footprint - Public Cloud.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Platform management]

- Turbonomic installation on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) : This release introduces support for installing Turbonomic on an AKS cluster that meets specific requirements. For more information, see Turbonomic installation on an AKS cluster.
- Extractor component enabled by default : The extractor component streams data to a standard format, supporting integrations such as embedded reporting and data exporter. This component is now enabled by default and you do not have to manually enable it in your Turbonomic custom resource file. The extractor uses minimal resources until you enable one of the integrations that it supports. For more information about enabling these integrations, see Enabling the Data Exporter and Enabling embedded reporting.

If you do not plan to use embedded reporting or the data exporter and want to disable the extractor component, add the following code to your custom resource file:

```
extractor: enabled: false
```

- Backoff mechanism for failing actions : Actions that repeatedly fail now enter a cooldown period that grows exponentially with each additional failure. This mechanism improves system stability by helping to mitigate issues that are caused by transient errors or misconfiguration, and prevents repeated failed actions from overloading the platform. For more information, see Intelligent backoff for failing actions.
- Firewall rules for IBM Enhanced Customer Data Repository (ECuRep) and IBM Blue Diamond : If you run your Turbonomic deployment behind a firewall, and need to share diagnostic data with support, you must add the required URLs and their ports to the firewall allowlist.
- IBM ECuRep
- -Follow the required firewall configuration as described in this IBM Support article.
- -Add the following AWS S3 endpoint to the allowlist:

```
Host URL: s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
```

- IBM Blue Diamond

Add the following endpoints to the allowlist:

- -Host URL: msciftpgw.im-ies.ibm.com [Port: 22]
- -Host URL: s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Versioning explanation]

Turbonomic versioning uses V-R-M elements (Version, Release, Modification) in the version number to express the status of a release.

| Numbered element                                           | Example   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| V - Version number                                         | 8 .X.X    | • Changes to platform architecture or significant changes to data models                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| R - Release number                                         | X. 2 .X   | • Major feature changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| M - Modification number is 0 (zero)                        | X.X. 0    | • A quarterly release • All Private Preview features from previous bi-weekly releases are now GA • No new Private Preview features in this release                                                                                                                                                   |
| M - Modification number is greater than zero (1 or higher) | X.X. 3    | • A bi-weekly release • Can include new Private Preview features • Includes fixed issues Note: For API developers, the X.X.1 release can include final implementations of deprecated API features. These final implementations can make API changes that are not compatible with an earlier version. |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Transport Layer Security requirements]

By default, Turbonomic requires Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.2 to establish secure communications with targets. Most targets have TLS 1.2 enabled; however, some targets do not enable TLS or they enabled an earlier version. In that case, you see handshake errors when Turbonomic tries to connect with the target service. When you go to the Target Configuration view, you see a Validation Failed status for such targets.

NetApp filers often do not enable TLS and the supported version is TLS 1.0, which causes the NetApp target to fail validation.

If target validation fails because of TLS support, you see validation errors with the following strings:

- No appropriate protocol

Ensure that you enable the latest version of TLS that your target technology supports.

- Certificates do not conform to algorithm constraints

Refer to the documentation for your target technology (such as the NetApp documentation) for instructions to generate a certification key with a length of 1024 or greater on your target server.

Because the API is a full reflection of the Turbonomic product, some changes to the product necessarily cause changes in the API. This can include bug fixes and improvements to the product. For example, new

commodities that you can get for a given entity type may be added, or a bug fix might change the data that is returned by an API request. IBM strives to make these changes backward-compatible whenever possible.

In some instances, changes that are not backward-compatible must be made. In this case, the change is deprecated for a period of time that should be sufficient for you to understand the change and implement an alternative in your scripts.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Minimum requirements]

The requirements for running a Turbonomic instance depend on the deployment method and the size of the environment you are managing.

Turbonomic keeps a real-time representation of your environment in memory. The greater the number of entities to manage, and the more extensive the relationships between them, the more resources you need for the VM that runs Turbonomic. As the VM requirements increase, so do the requirements for the physical machine that hosts the VM.

The requirements that are listed for each deployment method are recommendations that you should keep in mind as you plan your Turbonomic deployment. After deploying Turbonomic, if you need to change memory capacity, CPU capacity, or both for the VM, you can shut it down, make changes, and then power it up again to use the new capacity.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

The machine that hosts the Turbonomic platform must support the SSE4.2 instruction set. Support for this instruction set was introduced at different times for different chip manufacturers:

- Intel: November 2008
- AMD: October 2011

The machine that hosts Turbonomic should be newer than these dates. On a Linux system, you can run the following command to check for this support:

```
cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep sse4
```

For more information, see the glossary entry at http://www.cpu-world.com/Glossary/S/SSE4.html.

Usually you can run Turbonomic on a host that meets the following minimum requirements:

| Supported VMImage technology   | Supported VMImage technology                              | Storage requirements                                                                                                 | Memory                                                                                                                                               | CPUs     |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|
| VMware Microso ft              | vCenter versions 7.0 and 8.0 Hyper-V Server 2012 R2 later | 1.75 TB or greater (using Thin provisioning or Thick provisioning) Note: The /var partition must be at least 340 GB. | • Default: 160 GB • For 10,000 VMs or less, 96 GB Note: If you plan to install a VM with 96 GB of memory, you must modify the default for VM memory. | 12 vCPUs |

Turbonomic provides a VM image (an OVA or VHD file) which is preconfigured with two hard disk drives. A minimum of 1.80 TB is necessary to ensure that the drives have the proper amount of space for storage.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Turbonomic VM image]

Turbonomic installs as a VM that runs the Rocky Linux 9 OS. For more information about Rocky Linux 9 OS, see https://wiki.rockylinux.org/rocky/version/.

For each new version, Turbonomic delivers a VM image (Open Virtual Appliance (OVA) or Virtual Hard Disk (VHD)) that you install to run the product. Typically, you install this image once, and for subsequent updates to Turbonomic you execute product updates on that installed VM. This means two things:

- Product updates patch new components of the Turbonomic application stack onto the same Rocky platform that you got when you originally installed the VM image. Product updates do not affect the underlying OS.
- Over time, you might learn of important security patches for the Rocky distribution. It is your responsibility to keep the OS up to date. You can install these patches on your Turbonomic VM whenever necessary.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Turbonomic updates]

Because Turbonomic continually and rapidly innovates and improves all aspects of this product, newer versions of this product are released every two weeks. For more information about installing updates, see Updating Turbonomic to a New Version.

Turbonomic installs as a Kubernetes cluster on the VM. When you do update the product, the update can change:

- The application stack

This comprises several components and services such as:

- Application services for the user interface, analysis, and other product components.
- The historical database.
- Probes, which are components that implement the different targets you can configure.

For a full list of components in the application stack, you can inspect the platform's cr.yaml file.

- Data stores

The installation configures persistent and ephemeral storage for the Turbonomic product to use.

- Cluster configuration and management services

This update includes Kubernetes Operator and associated Kubernetes configuration files.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

For minimum requirements, 160 GB of memory for the VM that hosts Turbonomic is recommended. However, if you plan to manage a smaller environment (10,000 VMs or less), you can install on a VM that provides 96 GB of memory.

If you plan to install a VM with 96 GB of memory, then you must modify the default for VM memory.

To install the Turbonomic OVA:

1. Download the Turbonomic installation package.

The email you received from IBM includes links to the Turbonomic download pages. You can get the installation package from there.

The installation package includes the turbonomic\_t8c-<version> -<XXXXXXXXXXXXXX> .ova file where <version> is the Turbonomic version number and <XXXXXXXXXXXXXX> is the timestamp.

The OVA file deploys as a VM with the Turbonomic components already installed.

2. Import the OVA file into your datacenter.

Use the vCenter Server client to import the OVA into your environment.

3. Deploy the Turbonomic VM.

Configure the VM that was deployed from the OVA file.

If you want to deploy a VM with 64 GB of memory, manually modify the default value for Memory:

- a. Right-click the VM and select Edit Settings .
- b. Type 64 for Memory.
- c. Click OK to save the settings.
- d. Power on the VM.
4. Open the remote console.

For the Turbonomic VM that you just deployed:

- a. Choose the Summary tab.
- b. Click Launch Remote Console .
5. Set up the Turbonomic System Administrator account.
- a. In the remote console, log in with the following default credentials:
- Username: turbo

Do not use the account name, root .

- Password: vmturbo

Then, you will be prompted to enter a new password.

- b. Enter your new password.

The new password must comply with the strong password policy (a mixture of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and a symbol). Only you will know this new password.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

Be sure to save the changes account credentials in a safe place. For security reasons, this is the only account that can access and configure the Turbonomic VM.

- c. Enter your new password again to verify it.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Deploying the Turbonomic components]

After you install the Turbonomic VM that will host the platform, you can install the platform components.

First, gather the information that you need to run the installation:

- Network Time Source for Time Synchronization (optional)

You can complete this step during installation or later. If you want to synchronize the VM's clock now, you are prompted for the Network Time Source. For more information about synchronizing the VM's clock, see Synchronizing Time.

- Your updated root password

The installation script requires that you update the root password for the VM. If you followed the instructions in OVA: Installing the vCenter Image or in VHD: Installing the vCenter Image, then you have already completed this step.

When you are ready with the necessary information, you can run the installation script.

The IBM License Service, which collects license usage information that is used to create usage snapshots and reports, is installed automatically as part of the t8cinstall.sh script. For more information, see Tracking License Usage with IBM License Service.

The following steps describe the default installation process. If you want to customize your installation, then you should consider taking the steps in Stepwise Platform Deployment.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

IBM Container Registry is used for all Turbonomic images for online upgrades and installations. Ensure that you have access to https://*.icr.io before continuing.

All OVA installs use Kubernetes v1.28.8. Docker commands no longer work. You can use crictl and ctr commands instead. For more information, see the following resources:

- Container runtime changes in Kubernetes 1.28 and beyond on the Kubernetes documentation site
- Mapping from dockercli to crictl on the Kubernetes documentation site
- crictl command reference and information on GitHub
- ctr command reference and information on GitHub
1. Start up the installation script.
- Start a secure session (SSH) on your Turbonomic VM as the turbo user.
- Run the installation script.
2. Verify that you configured a static IP address for the Turbonomic VM.

```
/opt/local/bin/t8cInstall.sh
```

After the components start, you will type this static IP address into a web browser to access the login page for the Turbonomic user interface.

As a first step, the script prompts you with:

Have you run the ipsetup script to setup networking yet? [y/n] n

If you did not previously configure a static IP for the platform VM, the setup script will be called on so that you can configure a static IP, and continue the installation.

If you configured a static IP for the platform VM, enter y to continue the installation.

Because of dependencies between Turbonomic and the Kubernetes installation, it is not recommended to change the IP address after the Turbonomic installation. The VM must run with a static IP, regardless if this is a production, testing, or evaluation installation.

If you followed the instructions in OVA: Installing the vCenter Image or in VHD: Installing the vCenter Image, then you already ran the ipsetup script to configure a static IP.

3. Wait while the script completes the installation.

As the installation process continues, the script completes the following installation steps.

- Configures the platform environment with the necessary certificates.
- Configures the Kubernetes cluster on the VM.

Configuring the Kubernetes cluster can take a few tries before it succeeds. For each try that does not succeed, you see messages similar to:

To further debug and diagnose cluster problems, use 'kubectl cluster-info dump'.

When the connection succeeds, the script advances to the next steps.

- Establishes local storage for the platform.
- Creates the Kubernetes namespace for the platform as turbonomic .
- Configures authorization to access the required Kubernetes secrets.
- Initializes the MariaDB database server to manage historical data for the platform.

The script creates two accounts on the MariaDB that have full privileges:

- -root@localhost

This account does not use a password. To connect via this account the user must be system root .

- -mysql@localhost

This account does not use a password. To connect via this account the user must be system mysql .

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

For security reasons, Turbonomic recommends that you configure passwords for these accounts. You can connect with these accounts by using sudo . For example, sudo mysql . After you connect, you can then set passwords to these accounts. For more information, see the MariaDB Knowledgebase at https://mariadb.com/kb.

- Installs the Timescale database for embedded reports and the Data Exporter.
- Deploys and starts up the platform components.

As the deployment begins, the script prints the following:

```
############################ Start the deployment rollout ############################
```

After it deploys the components, it waits for the components to start:

```
The installation process is complete, waiting for all the components to start up.
```

```
** The script will wait for as long as 30 minutes. **
```

If the components all start within 30 minutes, then the installation is complete and successful.

If the components do not all start within 30 minutes, the script displays the following and then exits:

```
=========================================================================== One or more of your deployments has not started up yet. ** Please give your environment another 30 minutes to stablize. ** To check the status of your components, execute the following command: kubectl get pods If some components are still not ready, contact your support representative Deployments not ready:
```

The script then displays the formatted result of the kubectl get pods command. This shows you the status of the pods in the Turbonomic platform.

If the script exits before the components all start, give the platform another 30 minutes. To periodically check the component status, run the kubectl get pods command. If the components do not all start after another 30 minutes, contact your support representative.

If the installation is successful and all of the components started, the script displays a message similar to the following, where it gives the VM's static IP address:

```
################################################# Deployment Completed, please login through the UI https://10.10.123.123 #################################################
```

You can move on to the next steps.

4. Save a copy of the platform's Master Key secret.

The installation procedure creates a Master Key secret in the Kubernetes cluster. Turbonomic uses this secret to provide access for the platform components. Save the key data to a safe location.

To save the data:

- a. List the platform secrets.

```
kubectl get secrets
```

The results should include the Master Key secret.

```
... master-key-secret              Opaque                        1      57d ...
```

- b. Display the Master Key data.

After you find the Master Key name, you can then display the key data.

```
kubectl get secret master-key-secret -o yaml
```

The output is similar to the following example:

```

```

The important key data to save is the primary\_key... data. In this example, you should save the line:

```
primary_key_256.out: AfnJWutxNHAduaIOdAii3DRA2fMa6lzX4rWetZxxZvc=
```

- c. Save the data to a safe place.

Write this data to a file and save it in a safe backup location. If you ever need to recover the Master Key, your support representative uses this data to perform the recovery.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Installing on Kubernetes clusters]

Turbonomic is a containerized microservices platform that installs onto a Kubernetes cluster in a single namespace deployment. The platform uses an operator pattern to deploy, manage, and run the Turbonomic components. The Turbonomic platform operator ( t8c-operator ) uses a Custom Resource Definition (with an Xl kind) and a Custom Resource to configure and adjust your setup.

Currently, installation on Kubernetes clusters is supported on the Red Hat OpenShift platform, AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

kubernetes Node kubernetes Node

kubernetes Node turbonomic

3rd party

It is possible to install on any upstream compliant Kubernetes, but your Turbonomic representative might not be able to provide support.

As part of your deployment, you can take advantage of the backup and HA capabilities of an external database service running outside of the node cluster. - CLI (kubectl or oc)

- Container image repository (IBM icrio or

<!-- image -->

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Network]

The operator creates an NGINX LoadBalancer service by default, which uses an IP address or a load balancing service (external or internal), depending on the annotation.

Public IP and elastic load balancing are the default load balancers in the public cloud. However, it is recommended that you leverage one of the load balancers that is offered by the cloud provider, such as Network Load Balancer (NLB) or Application Load Balancer (ALB), and then configure the service annotations available for the chosen load balancer in the Turbonomic Custom Resource.

Since NGINX is deployed as a proxy service, you must edit the Custom Resource YAML to include NGINX attributes. Additionally, you can choose to have Turbonomic create a route in front of NGINX or you can manually create the route.

For more information, see NGINX Service Configuration Options and Platform Provided Ingress and Routes.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Container image repository]

Turbonomic supports public and private container image repositories. By default, the Turbonomic installation uses the public IBM Container Registry ( icr.io ).

To connect to icr.io , your environment must have direct access to the Internet or indirect access through a proxy server. If your environment is behind a firewall, make sure that you have full access to the IBM Container Registry services that deliver the Turbonomic components. You need to add https:// *.icr.io host address to your allowed firewall rules.

You can configure the installation to pull from a private repository and use pull secrets. For more information, see this topic.

For Red Hat OpenShift installations, if you are air-gapped or running a disconnected cluster and still want to use OperatorHub, see additional information in the Red Hat OpenShift documentation.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Storage]

The Turbonomic platform leverages persistent volumes (PVs) to store logs, certificates, and tokens. The platform uses Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) to create PVs from the cluster's default storage class, or a Security Context that is specified in the Turbonomic Custom Resource.

Recommendations and best practices:

- Use block storage for the PVs used by Turbonomic.
- Volume backup strategy is important. The PVs associated with the api , api-certs , auth , topologyprocessor , and consul-data PVCs should be backed up to ensure recovery in case of server loss. If you are running a containerized database for Turbonomic, back up db-data and datatimescaledb-0 .
- The following Storage Class properties are required:
- To support pods with multiple PVs, especially where your nodes are spread across multiple availability zones or regions, set the binding to be volumeBindingMode = WaitForFirstConsumer .
- Ensure recovery by setting the reclaimPolicy option of Retain .
- Ideally, also use a storage provisioner that allows for volume expansion ( allowVolumeExpansion ).

For PVC details and total storage required, see this topic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Resource recommendations for Kubernetes]

The amount of resources that you need to run Turbonomic is related to the complexity and type of entities that it manages. Entities include objects such as virtual machines, containers, pods, or cloud accounts. Turbonomic takes advantages of containers to scale the platform accordingly.

The following table provides a guideline to the cluster resources that you need to support the entities that you expect to manage in a single Turbonomic instance.

| Size   | Entity scale                             | Minimum size per node   | Number of nodes   | Estimated total memory consumption (GB)   | Estimated total CPU consumption (Cores)   |
|--------|------------------------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Small  | Up to 1,000 VMs 5,000 to 80,000 entities | 2 CPUs * 16 GB          | At least 3        | 8 to 42                                   | 3 to 6                                    |
| Medium | 1,000 to 16,000 VMs                      | 3 CPUs * 32 GB          | At least 3        | 32 to 91                                  | 4 to 9                                    |

| Size        | Entity scale                                         | Minimum size per node   | Number of nodes   | Estimated total memory consumption (GB)   | Estimated total CPU consumption (Cores)   |
|-------------|------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
|             | 80,000 to 200,000 entities                           |                         |                   |                                           |                                           |
| Large       | 16,000 to 40,000 VMs 200,000 to 1.5 million entities | 4 CPUs * 64 GB          | At least 4        | 50 to 110                                 | 7 to 16                                   |
| Extra large | 40,000 to 180,000 VMs Up to 2.1 million entities     | 4 CPUs * 96 GB          | At least 5        | 100 to 209                                | 10 to 20                                  |

Points to consider:

- For large or extra large deployments of , or if you need more then one instance, contact your Turbonomic representative for guidance and assistance.
- Turbonomic creates persistent volumes (PVs) based on dynamic storage provisioning. For more information, see this Storage class requirements.
- The total amount of memory and CPUs required depends on the number and type of enabled mediation components and configured targets. Each target type spins up its own pod.
- Turbonomic supports namespaces with resource quotas. Contact your Turbonomic representative for help in configuring a quota.
- For installations in the public cloud, do not use spot instances in the cluster where you install Turbonomic. Spot instances can be taken down at any time, which can then result in loss of access to Turbonomic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Option 2: NGINX as a LoadBalancer service type and customized annotations]

Turbonomic does not deploy an ingress controller. It deploys NGINX as a Kubernetes service, which can create a cloud provider load balancer. This load balancer has a type of external or can be used as an internal clusterIP service type that sits behind a customer/platform provided ingress.

It is assumed that you understand the following concepts:

- The types of load balancers that are available to you based on your cloud or infrastructure provider
- All service annotations that are available to you and which annotations are required for your environment

To modify the NGINX load balancer type service to use an internal IP address on your load balancer, use the required annotation according to your Kubernetes platform and version. Use an annotation that is applicable for your environment.

In the Turbonomic Custom Resource, you can specify the proper annotations that you determined are required for the load balancer for your NGINX service.

```
global: ingress: annotations: #provide the correct annotations based on the LB you want and the properties you want.
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > NGINX as proxy and 'bring your own' ingress or route]

You can configure nginx as a ClusterIP type service, allowing you to use your own ingress or route, and still maintain the Turbonomic internal routing rules and leverage nginx as a proxy. This is required to leverage embedded reporting on your Turbonomic instance.

1. Open the CR file for editing.

The location of the file depends on the type of Turbonomic installation that you are configuring.

- VM Image installation of Turbonomic

Log in to an SSH terminal session of your Turbonomic instance as the System Administrator that you set up when you installed Turbonomic.

```
/opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

- Turbonomic on a Kubernetes node or node cluster
2. Modify the CR file to set the nginxIsPrimaryIngress parameter to false .
3. Apply the changes that you made to the CR file.

```
deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

```
kind: XL metadata: name: xl-release spec: global: tag: 8.16.0 nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false #use the following parameters if you would like Turbonomic to create a single OCP route that will point to the nginx service #openshiftingress: #  enabled: true #nginxingress: #  enabled: true
```

For example, run the following command for VM image installations:

```
kubectl apply -f \ /opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Red Hat OpenShift routes and Turbonomic]

The following configuration deploys nginx as a proxy, and creates a single route that points to the nginx proxy:

```
kind: XL metadata: name: xl-release spec: global: tag: 8.16.0 nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false nginxingress: enabled: true openshiftingress: enabled: true
```

The name of the default route created will be nginx . To identify the hostname that you will use for your Turbonomic UI URL, while in the Turbonomic platform Project go to Networking > Routes and find the nginx route. The location for the route nginx is the Turbonomic UI URL.

Examples of the default location that is created include nginxyourNamespaceName.apps.yourOCPDomain .

This method creates a single route using a basic configuration with tls.termination: edge; tls.insecure, EdgeTerminationPolicy: Redirect, and using either the default ingress domain or one you define. Multiple routes are no longer created.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Pulling from a private repository]

To use your own private repository, you need to pull and stage Turbonomic images, which are located in the following repositories based on the deployment method. The components are the same regardless of the deployment method.

| Deployment method             | Default repositories                                                                |
|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Red Hat OpenShift OperatorHub | icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic icr.io/cpopen registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi- minimal |
| Direct deployment             | icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic icr.io/cpopen                                              |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Modifying the Turbonomic custom resource]

After the images are pulled in to your private registry, update the registry and repository location of the Turbonomic server container images in the custom resource yaml. Also update the Operator deployment yaml to pull from the registry.

Modify these values for your environment:

```
global: repository: <yourRegistry> / <yourRepository> _# uncomment line below if using RedHat Container Catalog, and specify `registry.connect.redhat.com/turbonomic` as the `repository`_ _# when deploying from the OCP Operator Hub the `repository` and `customImageNames` will be preconfigured for you_ # customImageNames: false _# for pull credentials, registry parameter is required and the value can be the same as repository_ _# uncomment what you need below if you need to specify pull credentials. Note this will be used for all images._ # registry: <yourRegistry> / <yourRepository> # imageUsername: turbouser # imagePassword: turbopassword # imagePullSecret: <yourSecret> tag: 8.16.0
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

If you are running the t8c-operator before version 42, you must define the registry and repository as shown in the following example:

```
global: registry: <yourRegistry> # imageUsername: turbouser # imagePassword: turbopassword # imagePullSecret: <yourSecret> repository: <yourRepository> tag:8.16.0
```

If you require credentials to access your registry, you can specify the username and password credentials as shown in the following example:

```
global: repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic registry: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic imageUsername: turbouser imagePassword: turbopassword # imagePullSecret: <yourSecret> tag: 8.16.0
```

- The registry parameter is required in the CR to use the imageUsername / imagePassword or imagePullSecret parameters.

- The customImageNames parameter must be set to false when working with Red Hat Operators and the Red Hat Container Catalog. You must also specify registry.connect.redhat.com/ turbonomic for both registry and repository .

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

When you deploy from the Red Hat OpenShift Operator Hub, these values are preset for you.

- This method creates a Kubernetes Secret of type docker-registry with the default name of turbocred . It then applies the pullSecret parameter to the Turbonomic component deployments.

Next, update the image: value in the Operator deployment yaml to pull from the repository.

```
containers: - name: t8c-operator image: <yourRegistry> / <yourRepo> /t8c-operator:42.78
```

If required, update the Turbonomic Operator to use the pull credentials. You can specify the image pull Secret in the Operator deployment yaml, or add this Secret to the t8c-operator service account.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

The registry parameter is required in the CR to use the imageUsername / imagePassword or imagePullSecret parameters.

Also add the Secret to the Turbonomic Operator deployment, which can be done in one of two ways.

1. Update the Operator deployment to use the Secret.
2. Link the Secret to the service account.

```
spec: serviceAccountName: t8c-operator imagePullSecrets: - name: <yourSecretName> containers: - name: t8c-operator
```

For the Operator, configure the t8c-operator service account for the image pull Secret. For more information, see the Kubernetes documentation.

In Red Hat OpenShift, run the oc secrets link command:

```
oc secrets link t8c-operator yourSecret -- for=pull
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Storage class requirements]

A persistent volume (PV) is a piece of storage in the Kubernetes cluster, while a persistent volume claim (PVC) is a request for storage. The Turbonomic platform uses persistent volumes to store logs, certificates, tokens, and some data for some of the services. It also dynamically provisions storage by using persistent volume claims to create PVs from the cluster's default storage class.

The following list outlines the recommended properties for a storage class. Follow the instructions for the storage provisioner that you are using.

- Use a dynamic storage provisioner; Turbonomic creates the PVC.
- Set Volume Expansion to be True .
- Set Reclaim Policy to Retain .
- Set Volume Binding Mode to WaitForFirstConsumer .
- Encryption is supported.
- Consider whether you want to use storage that is multi-zoned, but the cost will likely be more.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Best Practices]

- The Turbonomic platform relies on data that is stored in PVs that are important to retain target, licensing, and historical data association. Minimally you can use the reclaimPolicy option of Retain in the storage class. Back up the PVs associated with the following PVCs to aid in recovery if there is a loss of the server: api, api-certs, auth, and consul-data .
- Volume backup strategy is important. If you are running a containerized DB for Turbonomic, the embedded reporting feature, or both, include these PVs to preserve: db-data and datatimescaledb-0 .
- Use a storage class that allows for volume expansion ( allowVolumeExpansion ) for the DB PVs.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Non-default storage class]

The Turbonomic deployment uses the cluster's default storage class if one is defined. If you want to use a different storage class, specify the name of the storage class in the Turbonomic CR and apply the change.

1. Open the CR file for editing.

The location of the file depends on the type of Turbonomic installation that you are configuring.

- VM Image installation of Turbonomic

Log in to an SSH terminal session of your Turbonomic instance as the System Administrator that you set up when you installed Turbonomic.

/opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

- Turbonomic on a Kubernetes node or node cluster

deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

2. Modify the CR file to include the storage class.
3. Apply the changes that you made to the CR file.

```
global: repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic tag: 8.16.0 storageClassName: < yourStorageClass > externalIP: 10.97.96.3 pullPolicy: Always
```

For example, run the following command for VM image installations:

```
kubectl apply -f \ /opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

The following table describes the PVC resources and default configurations.

| Component          | Persistent volume claim   |   Size in Gi (default) | Notes                                                                        |

| api                | api                       |                      1 |                                                                              |
| api                | api-certs                 |                      1 |                                                                              |
| auth               | auth                      |                      1 |                                                                              |
| consul             | consul-data               |                      1 |                                                                              |
| db                 | db-data                   |                    500 | This component is not required when you use an external DB server or service |
| kafka              | kafka-log                 |                     50 |                                                                              |
| prometheus         | prometheus-server         |                      8 |                                                                              |
| redis(suspend)     | redis-data-redis-master-0 |                      4 | This component is required for the Parking feature.                          |
| rsyslog            | rsyslog-auditlogdata      |                     30 |                                                                              |
| rsyslog            | rsyslog-syslogdata        |                     30 |                                                                              |
| topology-processor | topology-processor        |                      3 |                                                                              |
| zookeeper          | zookeeper-data            |                      3 |                                                                              |
| timescaledb        | data-timescaledb-0        |                    125 | This component is required if embedded reporting is enabled.                 |

|             |                           |                        | Specify a new value for spec: postgresql: persistence: size: < value > Gi |

If you want to deploy with a different volume size, specify the volume in the Custom Resource. Combine these settings with any other properties specified. See the following example for db where the PVC size and Mem Limits are modified.

```
db: resources: limits: memory: 16Gi persistence: size: 500Gi
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Creating and configuring a remote database]

Before you install Turbonomic, you must configure a remote database server for historical data. This configuration allows for high availability, backups, and handling larger IO demands for larger environments or from remote SQL Server queries. If you are not going to use an existing database server, you must first create a new database server.

For its historical database, Turbonomic supports long-term maintenance stable series of MariaDB (the minimum supported version is 10.6) and MySQL 8.0.x. This support includes comprehensive testing and quality control for Turbonomic usage.

For more information, see Configuring a Remote Database.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Creating a project in the Red Hat OpenShift cluster]

This project is used throughout the installation process. The operator must be installed in this project (namespace).

1. Log in to your Red Hat OpenShift console and navigate to Home > Projects .
2. On the Projects page, click Create Project .
3. Specify the project name (for example, turbonomic ).
4. Click Create .
5. Determine the Security Context Constraints (SCC) UID range. This is used later in the install to allow pods to read and write to their PVs.
- a. Open the newly-created project from the Project page and click on the YAML tab.
- b. Find and make note of the Security Context Constraints (SCC) UID range.

You will see a SCC UID value similar to the following example. In this example, 1000680000 is the SCC UID value.

openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range:1000680000/10000

chunks.section_header: Creating a project in the Red Hat OpenShift cluster

chunks.text:
[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Installing Turbonomic using OperatorHub]

Install Turbonomic into the new project.

1. Navigate to Operators > OperatorHub .
2. In the Filter by keyword box, enter turbonomic to find and select the Turbonomic Platform Operator.

You will see multiple Turbonomic Platform Operator options. To install Turbonomic with a certified operator, ensure you select the "Certified" edition (do not select "Community" or "Marketplace" editions).

3. On the Turbonomic Platform Operator page, read the information about the operator and click Install .
4. On the Install Operator page, specify the Update channel, the project (Namespace) in which you want to install the operator, and the desired Update approval strategy.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

Ensure the Installed namespace is the same as the project you created earlier in the process.

Select Stable as the Update channel as it is the Generally Available tested product. The beta channel is a pre-release candidate and should not be used unless instructed.

Select Manual as the Update approval strategy so that you are alerted when a newer version of the operator is available.

5. Click Install .
6. Once the operator installs and you see "Installed operator - ready for use," click View Operator or select Operators > Installed Operators to view the Turbonomic Platform Operator.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

The custom resource can be accessed at any time during or after configuration by navigating to Installed Operators > Turbonomic Platform Operator > Turbonomic Platform Operator tab > xlrelease .

2. Set the server version and repository.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to change the repository parameter from the Red Hat Container Catalog to the IBM Container Registry ( icr.io/cpopen ).

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to include the version to install in the tag: <version to install> parameter as shown.

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic tag: <version to install>
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

The repository parameter must specify icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic as the repository location when working with Red Hat Operators.

3. Specify the external database properties.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to add the properties for the external database you created prior to installation, or remove the parameters to use a containerized database. Do one of the following:

- To use the external database IP address: Update the default externalDbIP value the IP address for your external DB server. If you use a fully qualified domain name for your DB Server, remove this parameter and use externalDBName instead.
- To use the external database name: Replace the externalDbIP parameter with the externalDBName parameter and include the database server's fully qualified domain name (for example, myDBServer.myDomain.com ).
- To use a containerized database: Remove the externalDbIP or externalDBName parameter. If neither are present, a containerized database is created.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

Using a containerized database is not supported as it can lead to irrecoverable data corruption. Additionally, a containerized database's performance is directly affected by network performance and cannot be guaranteed. A containerized database should be used for demo, Proof of Concept (POC), or testing purposes only.

The global section shown here is under the parent spec section of the custom resource. This example includes optional parameters and can be used as a guide for MySQL

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: {Edit this value with the IP address for your DB Server. If you use a fully qualified domain name for your DB Server, remove this parameter and use externalDBName instead. If you choose to use a containerized DB, this parameter should be removed} externalDBName: {If not using externalDbIP to specify your DB Server's IP address, use this parameter to specify your DB Server's fully qualified domain name, for example: myDbServer.myDomain.com} properties: global: enableSecureDBConnection: true sqlDialect: MYSQL dbPort: 6033 dbRootPassword: vmturbo dbRootUsername: turboadmin
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

Remove or comment out the sqlDialect parameter when using MariaDB, since MariaDB is the default database server type. Additional properties are required for AWS RDS and Azure DB Services. See documentation for configuring database app users, and provide that information here under properties: global in the parent spec section of the custom resource.

4. Set the Security Context Constraints to allow pods to read and write to their PVs. If this value is not set properly, the pods will not start up successfully.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to include the UID value you noted in step '5' on page 56 in the securityContext: fsGroup: parameter as shown in the following example:

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.0
```

5. Set up Turbonomic to automatically create a Red Hat OpenShift route to the nginx ClusterIP type Service. The Turbonomic operator can create a route for you that functions as the Turbonomic user interface and the endpoint for all remote probes, such as Kubeturbo configured on another cluster.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to include the nginx as shown in the following example. Change the default nginx from being a primary ingress to function as a proxy, then enable creating a route. The name of the default route that is created is nginx .

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.0 nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false nginxingress: enabled: true openshiftingress: enabled: true
```

(Optional) If you want to manually create your own route to Turbonomic/nginx use only the following parameters:

```
nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false
```

6. (Optional) If you are working with a private registry, and not the IBM Container Registry, edit the Custom Resource YAML to define registry and repository locations where the default is IBM Container Registry, and make the necessary changes to the operator deployment YAML.

Once the images are in your private registry, edit the repository parameter in the Custom Resource YAML to point to icr.io as the registry location.

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.0
```

If you require credentials to access your registry, you can specify either the image pull secret or the user name and password credentials in the Custom Resource YAML as shown in the following examples.

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 registry: myregistry repository: my.repo/myregistry/turbonomic imagePullSecret: turbocred securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.0
```

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 registry: myregistry repository: my.repo/myregistry/turbonomic imageUsername: turbouser imagePassword: turbopassword securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.0
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Note:]

- The registry parameter is required in the Custom Resource YAML to use the imageUsername/ imagePassword or imagePullSecret parameters.

- This will method creates a Kubernetes secret of type docker-registry with the default name of "turbocred," and then applies the imagePullSecret parameter to the Turbonomic component deployments.
- If using an imagePullSecret , a secret must be created and used instead of the imageUsername and imagePassword . These parameters should only be used when choosing not to utilize an imagePullSecret . See 'Container image repository and pull secrets' on page 49.
7. Click Create to create an instance of the Turbonomic Platform server.
8. When you first install Turbonomic using OperatorHub, target probes are disabled by default. Enable desired target probes, such as IaaS types whether on-prem or cloud.

A probe is a platform component that connects to a target. It discovers the target's entities and loads them into the Turbonomic supply chain, where actions can be executed on entities within the target environment. Turbonomic ships with many probe components that you can use to connect Turbonomic with your environment.

- a. Navigate to Installed Operators > Turbonomic Platform Operator > Turbonomic Platform Operator tab > xl-release .
- b. Edit the Custom Resource YAML to add and enable applicable targets for your instance. For a full description of supported targets, see Target Configuration.

You should not enable Kubeturbo in this step; it should be deployed into the monitored cluster in a separate project (namespace) and configured to communicate with Turbonomic. For more information, see this topic.

All target probes need to be configured in the custom resource using the formatting shown in the following example:

```
spec: global: tag: 8.16.0 ... aws: enabled: true azure: enabled: true dynatrace: enabled: true ...
```

- c. Save and apply your changes to the platform.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Validating the installation and completing setup]

1. Navigate to Workloads > Pods to confirm all pods are running and ready, for example 1/1, 2/2, and so on. This may take a few minutes.

If the pods do not run, review the following information for possible solutions:

- Ensure the Security Context Constraints UID is set correctly as noted in the preceding section then restart the pods.
- If you do not have access to the repository that is specified for the container images, check your credentials.
- Ensure the PVs are created and bound to the PVCs.
2. In the Turbonomic project, click Networking > Routes , select the nginx route (or the route you manually created), and click the Location field to open the address of your Turbonomic server (for example, nginx-yourNamespaceName.apps.yourOCPDomain ). This opens a new tab for the Turbonomic user interface.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Turbonomic installation on an AWS EKS cluster]

This topic provides an overview of the tasks that you need to perform to install Turbonomic successfully on an AWS EKS cluster. Turbonomic can be installed on any supported versions of EKS. For more information about supported versions of EKS, see Supported versions.

1. Review Turbonomic requirements for your AWS EKS cluster.

An AWS EKS cluster must be up and running and must meet certain requirements. For example, the cluster must be assigned an IAM role with the policies that Turbonomic requires and must have a specific number of nodes based on the size of your environment.

For more information, see this topic.

2. Install Turbonomic.

Turbonomic installation resources, such as the platform operator, custom resources (CRs), and custom resource definitions (CRD), are available for download from the IBM GitHub repository. The installation topic for AWS EKS describes these resources and how to deploy them as part of the installation.

For more information, see this topic.
section_path: Turbonomic installation on an AWS EKS cluster
chunks.section_header: Turbonomic installation on an AWS EKS cluster

chunks.text:
[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > AWS EKS cluster]

The AWS EKS cluster that you use for your Turbonomic installation must meet the following requirements:

| Item                                    | Requirements                                                                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cluster service role                    | Your EKS cluster must be assigned an IAM role that includes the following policies: • AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy • AmazonEKSServicePolicy • AdministratorAccess |
| Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnets | Use the default or create a new one.                                                                                                                          |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > AWS EKS cluster nodes]

The nodes in the AWS EKS cluster must meet the following requirements:

| Item                                           | Requirements                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Amazon Machine Image (AMI) type                | Turbonomic recommends nodes with the Managed Linux node type, which runs Amazon Linux applications on Amazon EC2 instances.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Node IAM role                                  | The nodes must be assigned an IAM role that includes the following policies: • AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy • AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly • AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Instance type                                  | • The instance type must have sufficient resources for Turbonomic to manage your environment. For guidance on the required resources based on the size of your environment, see this topic. • Do not use spot instances. Spot instances can be taken down at any time, which can then result in loss of access to Turbonomic. • Instance types running ARM-based processors (for example, AWS Graviton) are not supported. • Instance types running AWS Fargate are not recommended . |
| Available storage for persistent volumes (PVs) | At least 150 GB is required to support all PVs. For more information, see 'General requirements for persistent volumes' on page 53.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Node group scaling configuration               | The cluster to which you install Turbonomic must have at least three worker nodes. For guidance on the number of nodes to create based on the size of your environment, see this topic.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Other requirements]

If you are planning to add AWS targets in Turbonomic to optimize the performance of workloads, you must set up an IAM role or IAM user for the target connection.

For more information, see 'Overview of required AWS IAM identities for Turbonomic' on page 476.


## Next step

Install Turbonomic on AWS EKS.


## Installing Turbonomic on AWS EKS

This topic describes the steps to install Turbonomic on an AWS EKS cluster.


## Installation requirements

Before installing Turbonomic, be sure to review the installation requirements outlined in this topic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.0 > Downloading and deploying the resources for the operator]

The following steps set up credentials and a CRD to deploy the operator. These resources are namespaced, and you only need to be the administrator of your namespace (project).

1. Download and deploy an operator service account.

kubectl create -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/t8c-operator/main/deploy/ service\_account.yaml -n turbonomic

2. Run the following commands to download and deploy the cluster role and role binding instructions.

- Cluster role

kubectl create -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/t8c-operator/main/deploy/ cluster\_role.yaml -n turbonomic

This cluster role has sufficient privileges to manage Prometheus and Turbonomic as a business application (also known as Turbo-on-Turbo ).

- Cluster role binding

kubectl create -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/t8c-operator/main/deploy/ cluster\_role\_binding.yaml -n turbonomic
