[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Sample use cases]

VMem utilization for a Virtual Machine over time:

This query returns all the VM memory metrics that are collected for a specified virtual machine for a time interval. The time interval is truncated to the hour.

```
SELECT m.time, avg(m.utilization) AS avg_util FROM  metric m, scope_to($__timeFrom()::timestamptz - INTERVAL '24 hour',  date_trunc('hour', $__timeTo()::timestamptz), 'VIRTUAL_MACHINE', ARRAY[0]::bigint[], '0' = '0') s WHERE m.entity_oid = s.oid and m.time BETWEEN s.from_time AND s.to_time AND m.type = 'VMEM' AND m.provider_oid IS NULL AND m.time BETWEEN $__timeFrom()::timestamptz - interval '24 hour' AND date_trunc('hour', $__timeTo()::timestamptz) GROUP BY 1
```

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Storage Amount of Physical Machines Running On a Cluster:]

This query returns the max values of storage amounts for all the physical machines running in a cluster. The only parameter that is given to the query other than the time range is the cluster\_id . An internal function in Postgres can convert the cluster\_id to all the OIDs of the physical machines.

```
SELECT date_trunc('day', m.time) as time, m.entity_oid, MAX(current) FILTER (WHERE m.type = 'STORAGE_AMOUNT') as stor_used, MAX(capacity) FILTER (WHERE m.type = 'STORAGE_AMOUNT') as stor_cap, MAX(current) FILTER (WHERE m.type = 'STORAGE_PROVISIONED') as stor_prov FROM metric m, scope_to($__timeFrom(), $__timeTo(), 'STORAGE', ARRAY[$CluserId+0]::bigint[], $CluserId = '0') s WHERE m.entity_oid = s.oid AND m.time BETWEEN s.from_time AND s.to_time AND m.type in ('STORAGE_AMOUNT', 'STORAGE_PROVISIONED') AND m.time between $__timeFrom() and $__timeTo() GROUP BY 1, 2
```

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Physical Machine Average Memory Utilization - Week Over Week By Day:]

Returns the average daily memory utilization for virtual machines both for the current week and the past week.

```
WITH metrics AS ( SELECT m.time, m.utilization FROM metric m, scope_to($__timeFrom()::timestamptz - INTERVAL '7 day', $__timeTo(), 'PHYSICAL_MACHINE', ARRAY[0]::bigint[], '0' = '0') s WHERE m.entity_oid = s.oid AND m.time BETWEEN s.from_time AND s.to_time AND m.type = 'MEM' AND m.time BETWEEN ($__timeFrom()::TIMESTAMPTZ - interval '7 day') AND date_trunc('day', $__timeTo()::TIMESTAMPTZ) GROUP BY m.time, m.entity_oid, m.utilization ), DATA AS ( SELECT m.time, avg(m.utilization) AS avg_util FROM metrics m GROUP BY m.time ) SELECT INTERVAL '1 DAY' + CASE WHEN time BETWEEN date_trunc('day', $__timeFrom()::TIMESTAMPTZ - interval '7 day') AND date_trunc('day', $__timeTo()::TIMESTAMPTZ - interval '7 day') THEN date_trunc('day', time + interval '7 day') ELSE date_trunc('day', time) END as "time", CASE WHEN time BETWEEN date_trunc('day', $__timeFrom()::TIMESTAMPTZ - interval '7 day') AND date_trunc('day', $__timeTo()::TIMESTAMPTZ - interval '7 day') THEN 'Previous Week' ELSE 'Week Ending ' || DATE($__timeTo()::TIMESTAMPTZ)::TEXT END as metric, avg(avg_util)
```

```
FROM data GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
```

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Representation of Powered Off Virtual Machines:]

Ideally, metrics of a turned off virtual machine are still written on the table, assuming that the probe sends them in the entity dto. Most used values for commodities have NULL values, instead of having 0's. This configuration is needed to not affect potential averages over time, while the capacity has the same value, independent of the state of the machine. Still, some used values for commodities aren't NULL, such as storage, since the machine consumes those commodities even in a powered off state.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > pending\_action table]

This table lists the latest actions that have been recommended by the market. The table repopulates at a configurable interval (not necessarily every 10-minute market cycle). When it repopulates, all actions are replaced with the latest action recommendations.

This table does not include actions that are in progress.

| Data Object         | Type                     | Nullable   | Primary   | Description                                                                                                                              | Reference       |

| involved_entities   | bigint[]                 | True       | False     | An array of IDs for all the entities involved in the action. Includes the target entity.                                                 |                 |
| description         | text                     | False      | False     | The text description of the action.                                                                                                      |                 |
| savings             | double precision         | False      | False     | The cost savings this action results in. A negative savings indicates an investment.                                                     |                 |

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Scope table]

The Scope table tracks the association of two entities as they are related in each other's scope. The seed\_oid identifies the containing entity (the entity that defines the scope), and the scoped\_oid identifies the entity that is within the scope. This table updates with each market cycle.

| Data object   | Type   | Nullable   | Primary   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                 | Reference   |
|---------------|--------|------------|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| seed_oid      | bigint | False      | True      | The ID of the entity whose scope is the subject of the given record. For example, for a cluster-to-host relationship, the seed can be the cluster, and the scoped entity would be the host. |             |
| scoped_oid    | bigint | False      | True      | ID of the entity that is part of the seed scope.                                                                                                                                            |             |

| Data object   | Type                     | Nullable   | Primary   | Description                                                                                                                                                        | Reference   |
|---------------|--------------------------|------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| scoped_type   | enum                     | False      | False     | Entity type for the scoped entity.                                                                                                                                 | entity_type |
| start         | timestamp with time zone | False      | True      | When this relationship first appeared in the topology. This covers the initial appearance, or an appearance after a gap (the relationship was temporarily broken). |             |
| finish        | timestamp with time zone | False      | False     | When this relationship last appeared in the topology. A value of 9999-12-31T23:59:59 means the relationship is not yet known to have terminated.                   |             |

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Example 1:]

|   seed_oid |   scoped_oid | scoped_type       | start                 | finish               |
|------------|--------------|-------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|
|        111 |          999 | PHYSICAL_MACHI NE | 2021-01-01T05:0 0:00Z | 9999-12-31T23:5 9:59 |
|        999 |          111 | COMPUTE_CLUSTE R  | 2021-01-01T05:0 0:00Z | 9999-12-31T23:5 9:59 |

The first row indicates that cluster\_1 (oid: 111) contains Physical Machine\_1 (oid: 999). The start time indicates the first time that the entity was discovered. This relationship is ongoing and is represented by a finish timestamp of 9999-12-31T23:59:59. Row 2 shows that Physical Machine\_1 is contained by Cluster\_1.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Example 2:]

|   seed_oid |   scoped_oid | scoped_type       | start                 | finish                |
|------------|--------------|-------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
|        111 |          999 | PHYSICAL_MACHI NE | 2021-01-01T05:0 0:00Z | 2021-01-31T05:0 0:00Z |
|        999 |          111 | COMPUTE_CLUSTE R  | 2021-01-01T05:0 0:00Z | 2021-01-31T05:0 0:00Z |
|        222 |          999 | PHYSICAL_MACHI NE | 2021-01-31T05:0 0:00Z | 9999-12-31T23:5 9:59  |
|        999 |          222 | COMPUTE_CLUSTE R  | 2021-01-31T05:0 0:00Z | 9999-12-31T23:5 9:59  |

These records show that Physical\_Machine\_1 moved to Cluster\_2 (oid: 2222) on January 31. The timestamp for the end of the relationship with Cluster\_1 is the same as the timestamp for the start of the relationship with Cluster\_2.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Count Physical Machines in Clusters Over A Given Time Interval]

```
WITH all_relationships AS ( select e.name cluster_name, s.seed_oid cluster_oid, s.scoped_oid pm_oid FROM entity e
```

```
JOIN scope s on e.oid = s.seed_oid
```

```
and s.scoped_type ='PHYSICAL_MACHINE' WHERE e.type = 'COMPUTE_CLUSTER' AND ('2021-02-01T05:00:00Z','2021-02-18T04:59:59Z') OVERLAPS (s.start, s.finish) ), non_duplicate_relationships AS ( --    The same relationships between 2 entities can exist in given time interval if they move in and out of each others scopes --   these duplicates entries at varying time intervals are accounted for select * from all_relationships GROUP BY cluster_name, cluster_oid, pm_oid ) select cluster_name, count(*) from non_duplicate_relationships group by cluster_name
```

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Configuring an external TimescaleDB]

You can configure External Reports to use an external deployment of TimescaleDB. You can use this as an alternative to the default deployment.

To enable an external deployment, you must complete the following tasks:

- Deploy or access an external TimescaleDB instance. This instance is a PostgreSQL server with the TimescaleDB extension installed. The DB server must be deployed in a way that is accessible to your installation of Turbonomic. It can be deployed on the cloud or in an on-prem VM. As of Turbonomic 8.14.2, the embedded reports feature currently supports PostgreSQL 15.x and TimescaleDB 2.17.1. Prior to Turbonomic 8.14.2, the embedded reports feature supported PostgreSQL 12.x and TimescaleDB 2.10.2. For more information, see the following resources:
- Creating an External TimescaleDB
- Install TimescaleDB
- Provision users, databases, and schemas on the TimescaleDB instance. To provision these database objects, you can manually provision or enable Turbonomic to automatically provision. For more information, see:
- Manual provisioning of users and databases
- Automatic provisioning of users and databases
- Edit properties in the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file. The location of the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file depends on whether you are configuring an OVA installation or a Kubernetes Node installation of Turbonomic.
- Optionally, enable secure connections between Turbonomic and the TimescaleDB instance. For information about enabling TLS/SSL for database connections, see the PostgreSQL documentation Secure TCP/IP Connections with SSL.

This link provides steps to create a self-signed certificate that works with embedded reporting. However, self-signed certificates are not recommended for production instances.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Creating an external TimescaleDB]

You can create an external TimescaleDB service that you host in your environment. Alternatively, you can use an existing TimescaleDB service that is deployed on the cloud or in your enterprise by the DB Management team.

The TimescaleDB service that Turbonomic uses must satisfy these conditions:

- Deployment : The TimescaleDB is a PostgreSQL server with the TimescaleDB extension. It must be deployed in a way that is accessible to your installation of Turbonomic. It can be deployed on the cloud or in an on-prem VM.

For information about installing Timescale, see Install TimescaleDB.

- Supported version : As of Turbonomic 8.14.2, the embedded reports feature currently supports PostgreSQL 15.x and TimescaleDB 2.17.1. Prior to Turbonomic 8.14.2, the embedded reports feature supported PostgreSQL 12.x and TimescaleDB 2.10.2.
- An account with global R/W privileges on the TimescaleDB instanceTurbonomicThe embedded reports feature requires a specific set of databases to be created on the TimescaleDB instance. It is typical practice for an administrator to manually create the necessary databases. Alternatively, you can create a global R/W user account for the Turbonomic platform so it can create the databases automatically.
- Entry point : The TimescaleDB must provide an entry point through a DNS Name or IP address that you can access from Turbonomic. You configure this access in the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file.

To create the TimescaleDB, complete the following tasks:

1. Install the DB package. For information about installing Timescale, see Install TimescaleDB.

2. Create a global R/W user account that can be used to create databases on the DB service.

For information about automatically creating databases and users through R/W access, see Automatic Provisioning of Users and Databases.

3. Optional: Manually create the users and databases that embedded reports use.

If you cannot grant Turbonomic global R/W access to the DB, you must manually create the databases and users for embedded reports.

For information about manually creating databases and users, see Manual Provisioning of Users and Databases.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Manual Provisioning of users and databases]

For Turbonomic to automatically create the required databases for embedded reports, the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file must specify credentials for a user account that has global R/W access to the DB service. To ensure this access, you can store the credentials in cleartext in the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file.

If Automatic Provisioning is appropriate for your environment, then you can go directly to Automatic Provisioning of Users and Databases. That topic is where you specify the global R/W account that embedded reports can use to access your TimescaleDB.

If Automatic Provisioning is not appropriate for your environment, you must access the DB service with an R/W account and manually add the databases and user accounts that embedded reports can use. Then, after you add the databases to your TimescaleDB, you will edit the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file to use these databases.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Manually provisioning databases and users on the TimescaleDB]

The following steps provision the database objects that embedded reporting requires. These examples use default names for illustration. You can substitute your own names for databases and users. Remember the names that you use because you must match them as you edit the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file.

To provision the databases and users, open a command session on the TimescaleDB, and run the following commands:

- Create two databases - one for extractor data, one for grafana data: The extractor database manages the Turbonomic data stream, and the Grafana database manages data for reporting within Grafana.

Run the following commands, where you can specify your own database names instead of extractor and grafana :

```
CREATE DATABASE extractor; CREATE DATABASE grafana;
```

- Create database users: For the extractor database, you create an R/W user, a read-only group, and a read-only user. Also create an R/Wn user for the Grafana database.

Run the following commands, where you can specify your own names for instances of USER or ROLE :

```
-\- main read/write user for extractor data CREATE USER extractor PASSWORD '<password>'; -\- group for users with read-only access to extractor data CREATE ROLE readers_extractor_extractor; -\- read-only user for extractor data as a member of that group CREATE USER query PASSWORD '<password>'; GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE extractor TO readers_extractor_extractor; GRANT readers_extractor_extractor TO query; -\- read-write user for grafana data CREATE USER grafana_backend PASSWORD '<password>';
```

- Create and prepare the schema for extractor data. Connect to the extractor database and run these commands, where you can specify your own name for the SCHEMA , and you grant privileges to the users and roles you previously created:
- Create and prepare the schema for Grafana data. Connect to the Grafana database and run these commands, where you can specify your own name for the SCHEMA , and you grant privileges to the users and roles you previously created:

```
CREATE SCHEMA extractor; -\- read/write user has full access GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA extractor TO extractor; -\- all users in readers group have read-only access GRANT USAGE on SCHEMA extractor TO readers_extractor_extractor; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA extractor TO readers_extractor_extractor; -\- make sure readers get access to any tables added in the future ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA extractor GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO readers_extractor_extractor; -\- make the extractor and query users use the extractor schema by default ALTER ROLE extractor SET search_path TO `extractor`; ALTER ROLE query SET search_path TO `extractor`; -\- install the timescaledb plugin into the extractor database using the extractor schema CREATE EXTENSION timescaledb SCHEMA extractor;
```

```
CREATE SCHEMA grafana; -\- read/write user has full access GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA grafana TO grafana_backend; -\- make sure the grafana user uses the grafana schema by default ALTER ROLE grafana_backend SET search_path TO 'grafana';
```

The previous commands provision the required databases and users. Your provisioning must be complete and correct for embedded reports to properly collect data and display it in Grafana reports and dashboards.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Editing the CR file for manually created databases]

After you provision the required database objects, edit the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file to use these databases.

To edit the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file:

1. Open the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file for editing.

The location of the file depends on the type of Turbonomic installation that you are configuring:

- For an OVA installation of Turbonomic:

Open an SSH terminal session on your Turbonomic instance.

Log in with the System Administrator that you set up when you installed Turbonomic:

- Username: turbo
- Password: <your\_private\_password>

Then edit the file:

/opt/Turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

- Turbonomic on a Kubernetes node or node cluster:

Open the following file for editing:

deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

2. Specify the endpoint for connecting to the external database.

You can use the database service DNS, or you can use an IP address.

Add the endpoint as the externalTimescaleDBIP property in the spec: global: section of the .cr file:

```
spec: global: externalTimescaleDBIP: <host-or-IP>
```

3. Specify Turbonomic access to the databases that you provisioned.

As you specify users and databases, be sure to match the names you used to provision users, databases, and schema. These instructions use the default naming.

You specify:

- Global read-only access to the extractor database /spec/properties/global/dbs This grants the extractor and the api components read-only access to the extractor database that you previously provisioned. Those components use the query user account.
- Read/write access to the extractor and grafana databases /spec/properties/ extractor/dbs This grants the extractor component read/write access to the extractor and grafana databases that you previously provisioned.
- Read/write access for Grafana to access the grafana database /spec/grafana/grafana.ini/ database

Edit the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file to add the following entries:

```
spec: properties: global: dbs: extractor: databaseName: extractor schemaName: extractor query: userName: query password: <defaault-password> extractor: dbs: extractor: userName: extractor password: <default-password> grafana: schemaName: grafana grafana: grafana.ini: database: name: grafana user: grafana_backend password: <default-password>
```

4. (Recommended) Block automatic provisioning by Turbonomic on the TimescaleDB.

If you manually provisioned the embedded reports objects on the TimescaleDB instance, disable the options for Turbonomic to automatically run provisioning on the TimescaleDB instance.

chunks.text:
[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Note:]

Turbonomic cannot provision on the TimescaleDB instance if you do not specify a global user account.

Set the following properties to false :

- shouldProvisionDatabase : spec/properties/global/dbs/postgresDefault/ shouldProvisionDatabase Determintes whether Turbonomic attempts to provision any database in scope of the definition.
- shouldProvisionUser : spec/properties/global/dbs/postgresDefault/ shouldProvisionUser Determines whether Turbonomic attempts to provision any logins in scope of the definition.
- destructiveProvisioningEnabled : spec/properties/global/dbs/postgresDefault/ destructiveProvisioningEnabled Determines whether, during its provisioning operations, Turbonomic can perform destructive operations like dropping databases, schemas, or users that

are mis-configured. In the default installation scenario, the public schema that is created by PostgreSQL in any new database is dropped to reduce the complexity of the overall model. Because this operation is considered destructive, this option is true by default.

Edit the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file to add the following properties:

```
spec: properties: global: dbs: postgresDefault: shouldProvisionDatabase: false shouldProvisionUser: false destructiveProvisioningEnabled: false
```

Placing these settings in the /spec/properties/global/dbs/postgresDefault block ensures that they apply to all PostgreSQL databases and users who are used by any Turbonomic component. If your pre-provisioning is more selective, you can move the settings to more narrowly targeted property blocks like /spec/properties/extractor/dbs/grafana or /spec/properties/global/dbs/ extractor .

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Automatic provisioning of users and databases]

For Turbonomic to automatically create the required databases for embedded reports, the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file must specify credentials for a user account that has global R/W access to the DB service. To enable this access, store the credentials in cleartext in the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file.

If Automatic Provisioning is not appropriate for your environment , you must access the DB service with an R/W account and manually add the databases and user accounts that embedded reports can use. See Manual Provisioning of Users and Databases.

To enable an external TimescaleDB for embedded reports, you must edit the Turbonomic charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file.

1. Open the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file for editing.

The location of the file depends on the type of Turbonomic installation that you are configuring:

- For an OVA installation of Turbonomic:

Open an SSH terminal session on your Turbonomic instance.

Log in with the System Administrator that you set up when you installed Turbonomic:

- Username: turbo
- Password: <your\_private\_password>

Then edit the file:

/opt/Turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

- Turbonomic on a Kubernetes node or node cluster:

Open the following file for editing:

deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

2. Specify the endpoint for connecting to the external database.

For the connection endpoint, specify either the fully qualified domain name of the external server or its IP address.

Add the endpoint to the spec/global/externalTimescaleDBIP property in the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file:

```
spec: ...
```

```
global: externalTimescaleDBIP: <host-or-IP>
```

3. Specify the global R/W account that Turbonomic uses to log in to the TimescaleDB service.

This enables Turbonomic to automatically create the databases, schemas, and users that embedded reports requires.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Note:]

Only complete this step if you want to enable global RW access to the TimescaleDB service in the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file. You specify the account credentials in clear text.

If you choose not to specify the global account here, then you must manually provision the database objects that embedded reports requires. See Manual Provisioning of Users and Databases.

To grant the access Turbonomic needs, specify the username and password for an account that has global R/W privileges on the TimescaleDB instance. Add these credentials in the /spec/ properties/global/dbs/postgresDefault block of the cr.yaml file, as follows:

```
spec: properties: global: dbs: postgresDefault: rootUserName: <root-user> rootPassword: <root-password>
```

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Reference: Working with YAML files]

YAML is the primary file format to create and configure resources on kubernetes, including everything to do with the Turbonomic platform. The Custom Resource YAML provides a convenient, single place to define the majority of configuration details for Turbonomic. When editing YAML files, you must be careful to respect the file syntax, including indents in the file. General rules for edits include:

- Always uses spaces, not tabs, for all indentation. Since spacing and indentations matter, and can yield an invalid result or a parameter completely skipped over, you should work with YAML files with an editor that supports using vertical lines associated with indentations to visually spot a misalignment. If your editor of choice makes this difficult, you can use the linux expand utility when you're done, to convert tabs to equivalent spaces.
- Indention uses two spaces per level.
- Be careful to keep the same indentation for all properties in a given section.
- Never use the same property name twice in the same section. Doing this will render the YAML file invalid, though you will likely not see any notification of a problem. Rather, all but one of the property definitions will be silently ignored.

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Spacing matters]

For the Turbonomic Custom Resource, indentation defines where parameters are applied (globally or to specific components), so ensure you line up the text appropriately. The following example shows examples of specifications that are applied at a global level ( {'spec':{'global': [{'tag':'8.16.0'}]}} ) which sets the container image tag for all instances. Then indented you see properties that are global for the remote database ( {'spec':{'properties':{"global": [{'dbPort':'6033'}]}}} ) describes a property of dbPort that would be set for remote DB connections.

Each line is indented two spaces from the higher level.

```
spec: global: repository: turbonomic tag: 8.16.0 properties: global:
```

```
dbPort: 6033 kubeturbo: enabled: true aws: enabled: true
```

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Combine properties correctly]

A YAML file is read beginning to end, and if there are different parameters that apply to the same component, they need to be combined. The following example shows a YAML where properties for the ui component of image tag and memory limit resources.

```
spec: global: repository: turbonomic tag: 8.16.0 ui: image: tag: 8.16.0 properties: global: dbPort: 6033 kubeturbo: enabled: true aws: enabled: true ui: resources: limits: memory: 4Gi
```

This YAML will not set both image tag and memory limit resources for the ui component because they are set in two different sections. The memory limits would be applied since that is the last section to be read, and it would overwrite the first set of properties with the image tag. The following YAML will set both image tag and memory limit resources for the ui component:

```
spec: global: repository: turbonomic tag: 8.16.0 ui: image: tag: 8.16.0 resources: limits: memory: 4Gi properties: global: dbPort: 6033 kubeturbo: enabled: true aws: enabled: true
```

To avoid having the same property name twice in the same section, search for an existing instance of the key you want to add. With the complex embedded structure in many k8s resources, this can be quite challenging; however, you can use an online validator that does not accept duplicate keys to check your entire CR file (such as YAMLint - The YAML Validator).

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Finding a property]

This documentation refers to specific properties in the CR file using a "path" expression. For example, assume the path /spec/global/repository to designate a repository property in the file. You can find the property in the file as follows:

1. Find a line that says spec: with no indentation at all.
2. Between that line and the next unindented line (not counting comments, which start with # ), find a line that says global: and is at the next level of indentation.

3. Between that line and the next line with the same indentation, find a line that starts with repository: . That line is where the addressed property is defined.

In this example, find the repository property specified by /spec/global/repository :

```
apiVersion: charts.helm.k8s.io/v1alpha1 kind: Xl metadata: name: xl-release spec: properties: global: repository:        # This is NOT the correct property ... # Global settings global: repository: # This is the one you want
```

The first repository property is not at /spec/global/repository , but at /spec/properties/ global/repository .

[Section: MCIDCIVCIDCICI > Chapter 15. Compliance]

Turbonomic adheres to a number of standard certifications. Turbonomic is part of the IBM Cloud Services ISMS ISO 27001:2013, 27017:2015, 27018:2014, and 27701:2019 certification program. The ISO standards specify the requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an information security management system. They also include requirements for the assessment and treatment of information security risks. See IBM Cloud compliance programs for more information. The IBM certificates are available online.

- ISO 27001 is a widely-adopted global security standard outlining the requirements for informationsecurity management systems and provides a systematic approach to managing company and customer information based on periodic risk assessments.
- ISO 27017 gives guidelines for information-security controls applicable to the provisioning and use of cloud services, as well as implementation guidance for both cloud service providers and cloud service customers.
- ISO 27018 establishes commonly accepted control objectives, controls, and guidelines for implementing measures to protect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) in accordance with the privacy principles in ISO 29100 for the public cloud computing environment.
- ISO 27701 provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving a Privacy Information Management System.

Turbonomic team reviews security and privacy-related activities for compliance with IBM requirements.

Assessments and audits are completed by the Turbonomic team to confirm compliance with its information security policies.

Workforce security education and awareness training is completed by the Turbonomic team on an annual basis. IBM personnel are reminded of their job objectives, and their responsibility to meet ethical business conduct and Turbonomic security obligations.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Chapter 1. Turbonomic 8.16.5 Documentation]

Documentation for this product release includes the following general topics.

- Release notes - Describes new features, improvements, deprecated/removed features, and known issues
- SaaS management - Helps you manage a SaaS server in the public cloud and, if needed, set up a SaaS client in your on-prem environment so that the SaaS server can manage your on-prem workloads
- Self-hosted installation - Helps you install and update Turbonomic in your on-prem environment
- Product overview - Provides an overview of the platform and its underlying architecture
- Getting started - Describes login steps, the Home Page, actions, and policies
- Target configuration - Provides a list of targets that the product can monitor, and describes how to configure each target properly
- User interface reference - Provides a list entities discovered from targets, and describes how to configure plans, charts, and administrative settings
- API reference - Helps you use the REST API as you script interactions with the product
- Integration - Data Ingestion Framework - Describes how to set up Data Ingestion Framework, a feature that enables you to define custom entities and entity metrics for your environment, and load them into the platform for analysis
- Integration - Data Exporter - Describes how to set up Data Exporter, a feature that streams Turbonomic data about entities and actions as JSON documents, and then publishes the data to a Kafka topic
- Integration - SaaS Reporting - Describes how to set up SaaS Reporting, a SaaS-based add-on that stores a history of your managed environment and presents this history via Liveboards and reports
- Integration - Embedded Reporting - Describes how to set up Embedded Reporting, an add-on that stores a history of your managed environment and presents this history via dashboards and reports

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Release date : July 09, 2025]

These release notes describe new features, updates, configuration requirements, and other important information for Turbonomic 8.16.5.

To update to version 8.16.5, your Turbonomic version must be at least 8.9.0. If you currently run an earlier version of Turbonomic, you must update to version 8.9.0 first. For assistance in updating to version 8.9.0, contact your Turbonomic representative.

To view the release notes for earlier versions of the product, visit this page.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Version 8.16.5]

- Parking actions for workload sets : You can now define workload sets in Turbonomic. A workload set is a group of parkable workloads that can be managed together for parking operations. For example, if you have database servers and virtual machines that are part of the same application, you can park them together as a workload set and configure the parking order to ensure a graceful shutdown. For more information, see Workload sets.
- Support for Azure reservations scoped to resource groups : Azure reservations that are scoped to resource groups are now supported, enabling them to be considered in resource analysis and action generation. Application of reservations coverage during analysis will only apply to workloads within the resource group. For more information, see Discount inventory chart.
- Discovery of Google Cloud unmanaged instance groups : Turbonomic now discovers Google Cloud unmanaged instance groups and adds them to the Groups category on the Search page. Use UnmanagedInstanceGroup as your search keyword to view a list of unmanaged instance groups discovered in your environment.

Turbonomic does not support actions for unmanaged instance groups, but it supports scale and parking actions for individual VMs in a group. For scale actions, you can create a virtual machine policy that is scoped to an unmanaged instance group to apply the same action constraints and settings to all VMs in the group. For parking actions, a parking policy applies to individual VMs but not to an unmanaged instance group.

- Newly supported AWS instance types : This release introduces support for the following AWS instance types:
- -m7i and r7i for RDS database servers
- -m8g and r8g for EC2 virtual machines and RDS database servers with the Graviton4 processor

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Version 8.16.4]

- Top actions widget and Action Center view for cloud actions : This widget can help streamline decision-making by highlighting non-disruptive, high-impact actions that can be executed immediately,

prioritizing performance-related tasks. The widget ranks actions intelligently and displays a simple summary of the top five actions for the following categories: Highest value (combines performance with cost savings), Top performance, and Top savings. For more information, see Top actions chart.

- Discount-aware scale actions for Azure VMs : Turbonomic now accounts for Savings Plan for Compute coverage when recommending scale actions for Azure VMs. This ensures that scaling decisions reflect actual cost coverage, resulting in more accurate recommendations and cost impact analysis.
- Enhanced cost impact calculations for Azure VMs : For Azure VMs that are covered by Reservations or Savings Plan for Compute, Turbonomic now calculates the cost impact of scale actions based on the following cost metrics.
- -On-demand cost : The uncovered usage cost based on Azure's published on-demand rates and VM uptime.
- -Effective cost : A blended rate that includes on-demand cost and the amortized costs of Reservations and/or Savings Plans for Compute.

You can configure the Cost basis setting in the user interface to choose the cost metric that is shown by default in the Action Details page for an Azure VM scale action. For more information, see Cost basis.

Note: To enable this feature, add an Azure Billing target. Effective cost calculation is not supported for pay-as-you-go accounts.

- Execution Source filter in the Actions chart for cloud workloads : The Actions chart now includes the Execution Source filter to help you distinguish between actions executed in Turbonomic and externally (for example, in your cloud provider console or CLI). To use this filter, set the Actions chart type to Tabular and the primary filter to Executed Actions - Succeeded . For more information, see Actions chart.
- Reconfigure actions to enable hot add for vCenter VMs : Turbonomic now recommends reconfigure actions for vCenter VMs that are non-compliant with VM policies requiring vCPU and vMem hot add. When these actions are executed, hot add is automatically enabled for the VM.
- Discovery of Python applications from Application Performance Management (APM) targets : The following APM targets now discover Python application types and their associated commodities:
- Cisco AppDynamics
- Datadog
- Dynatrace
- Instana
- New Relic

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

The existing Parker role has been renamed Parking Administrator. This role includes all the Parking Automator privileges and the ability to manage parking schedules. After you update to this release, users with the Parker role automatically change their role name to Parking Administrator.

- Application type field for application components : A new Application type field has been added to the Entity Information widget for application components. This field appears on the Overview tab when viewing component details. The application type (such as Tomcat, Python, JVM, and more) is derived from metadata provided by the associated Application Performance Management (APM) target. If the application type cannot be determined, it shows as "Unknown". Supported APM targets for detecting application type include:
- Cisco AppDynamics
- Datadog
- Dynatrace
- Instana
- New Relic

You can use the Application type field as a search filter criteria when searching for application components. Values for the filter only display when at least one APM target is configured.

- Advanced configuration for Application Performance Management (APM) targets : A new Advanced configuration page is now available for configuring target-specific settings when creating or editing the following APM targets:
- Cisco AppDynamics
- Datadog
- Dynatrace
- Instana
- New Relic

Currently the following option is available for configuring these targets:

- -Display discovered virtual machines : Enable this option to allow Turbonomic to display virtual machines that are discovered through the APM target, even if they are not discovered by any related infrastructure targets. If this option is disabled, virtual machines that are discovered only by the target are not displayed.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Version 8.16.2]

- Execution Source filter in cloud savings and investments charts : As you execute actions for your public cloud workloads in Turbonomic or externally (for example, in your cloud provider console or CLI), Turbonomic tracks the impact of actions on performance and cost. The Realized Savings, Cumulative Realized Savings, Realized Investments, and Cumulative Realized Investments charts now include a filter called Execution Source so you can narrow down cost data to actions executed in Turbonomic or externally.
- Dynamic filter for on-prem VM reservation : Placement policies for initial placement of on-prem VMs now include dynamic filter restrictions. An on-prem VM reservation will be processed only if the selected VM template's attributes (CPU count, memory size, and storage) match the dynamic filters in the placement policy groups. This applies only to dynamic filters with any of these three attributes.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Version 8.16.1]

- Support for Azure Premium SSD v2 : Turbonomic now discovers Azure Premium SSD v2 managed disks. Turbonomic recommends scaling these managed disks to optimize performance at the lowest possible cost, or deleting them if they become unattached to reduce your cloud expenses.

The following actions can now be performed using Turbonomic:

- Delete
- Scale within the Azure Premium SSD v2 tier family

Actions to scale from Azure Premium SSD v2 to another tier family (and vice versa) are recommended only. Use the Azure portal or Azure CLI to execute these scaling actions.

- Controlled action generation for injected sidecars : You can now disable action generation for sidecar containers using a new configuration setting, disableActionGeneration . To take advantage of this feature, ensure that both Kubeturbo and Kubeturbo operator are updated to version 8.16.1.

This new configuration setting is backward compatible and the default mode is Recommended . If the new configuration setting is not added, action generation will be enabled by default for injected sidecars.

For more information, see Handling of resize actions for sidecar container specs.

- Migration of Place page : The Place page for managing reservations is now migrated to the new design for the user interface. For more information, see New design for the user interface.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Version 8.16.0]

- Application performance management
- -New underlying entity types for application maps : Starting with 8.15.3, you can create or update an application map that includes the following newly supported entity types and then view the corresponding supply chain:
- Application component spec
- Document collection
- Virtual machine spec

For more information, see Application map.

- -Support for .NET applications : Turbonomic can now discover and collect metrics from .NET applications on Datadog, Dynatrace, Instana and New Relic targets.
- -Simplified database password configuration for Oracle targets : You can now update Oracle database passwords in bulk by uploading a CSV file through the Turbonomic user interface. This feature enables IT Ops teams to regularly rotate their passwords for multiple Oracle targets without having to manually update each target. For more information, see Updating Oracle database passwords in bulk.
- -Removal of support for JBoss targets : As of version 8.15.1, Turbonomic no longer supports JBoss targets. After you upgrade to version 8.15.1 or later, delete any existing JBoss targets from the Target Configuration page by selecting the target and clicking Delete . Also, it is recommended that you delete jboss and mediation-jboss related settings from the Turbonomic Custom Resource (CR) file. For more information, see (Optional) Enabling and disabling probe components.
- Container platform resource management
- -Target configuration wizard for container platform targets : When you add a Kubernetes or Red Hat OpenShift target in the Target Configuration page, you will now see a Connect Target option that launches a target configuration wizard. This wizard streamlines the target deployment process by prompting for the required settings and generating a script. You can then download the script and run it in your Kubernetes or Red Hat OpenShift cluster to complete the deployment. For more information, see Deploying to a Kubernetes cluster and Deploying to a Red Hat OpenShift cluster.
- -Automation of scale actions for workloads managed by Knative Serving : Turbonomic can now automate scale actions for workloads managed by Knative Serving. Turbonomic automatically detects and updates the minimum and maximum replicas to the values configured in the Knative Service Custom Resource (CR). The Knative Serving controller then scales the workloads accordingly.

No additional setup is required to enable Knative Serving support in Turbonomic.

For more information, see Support for Knative Serving.

- -Multi-instance GPU (MIG) aware horizontal scale actions for Kubernetes GenAI LLM workloads : If your NVIDIA GPUs are partitioned using MIG, Turbonomic now recognizes the GPU partitions and recommends MIG-aware horizontal scale actions for Kubernetes GenAI LLM workloads accordingly. To generate scale actions, Turbonomic analyzes GPU metrics that Prometurbo collects from a customer-managed Prometheus instance. For more information, see MIG-aware horizontal scale actions.
- -New performance metric for container platform services that back AI workloads : For workloads running large language models in Kubernetes, Turbonomic now leverages a vLLM metric called percentage of KV cache usage ( vllm:gpu\_cache\_usage\_perc ). The Prometurbo agent for Turbonomic collects this metric from Prometheus and then continuously monitors it as a performance metric for container platform services. When you set Service Level Objectives (SLOs) in policies for these container platform services, Turbonomic can generate SLO-driven scale actions to prevent resource bottlenecks and maximize the performance of AI workloads, while keeping cache usage within the desired thresholds. For more information, see Container platform service policies.
- -Automated execution of resize up actions for container vCPU and vMem requests : Automated action execution is now supported for resize up actions for container vCPU and vMem requests. Previously, these actions were only manually executable in the Turbonomic user interface or directly in your container platform cluster. For more information, see Resizing resource limits and requests.
- -Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization target configuration : Turbonomic now discovers Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization resources through a new or existing target configuration with Red Hat OpenShift. For more information, see Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization.
- -Go-based operator for Prometurbo : Prometurbo now uses a Go-based operator to enable automatic changes to the Prometurbo deployment. With this improvement, you no longer need to update or delete resources manually.

For Prometurbo deployments in Red Hat OpenShift OperatorHub, the new Go-based operator is available as the certified edition in Prometurbo's stable channel. Prometurbo automatically switches from the Helm-based operator to the Go-based operator if your approval strategy is Automatic. If your approval strategy is Manual, OperatorHub notifies you that an operator update is available. Approve the update when you see the notification.

- On-prem resource management
- -Hot add for vMEM and vCPU : This release introduces new Enable vCPU hot add and Enable vMEM hot add settings for vCenter VMs in the on-prem VM policy settings. When these settings are enabled, Turbonomic can resize vCPU or vMEM for vCenter VMs without restarting the scoped VMs. You can enable hot add only for vCenter VMs that meet the following conditions:
- -Fault tolerance is not enabled.
- -VMware tools is installed.
- -Virtual hardware version is 11 or later.

The hot add feature is provided by vCenter and might be subject to other vendor limitations. For more information, see On-prem VM policies and the vCenter documentation.

- -Support for forcing minimum sizing for on-prem virtual machines : Turbonomic now supports configuring policies to take resize actions when virtual machines (VMs) are out of compliance. With this feature, you can bring the vCPU and vMem parameters of a VM into compliance by running the recommended compliance actions that are generated based on VM policies. You can also update policy settings to prevent compliance actions from being generated for specific VMs. With the availability of this feature, the listed generated resize actions for your VMs can now include compliance actions. For more information about this feature or updating your policy settings for generating compliance actions, see Forced minimum sizing for on-prem VMs.
- -Resize of on-premises VMs even when they are powered off : A new Resize when powered off setting in the on-premises VM automation policies enables Turbonomic to resize VMs even when they are powered off. This setting is useful in environments where powered-off VMs must be resized according to the anticipated load when they are restarted. This feature is available in vSphere, VMM, and Hyper-V environments. For more information, see On-prem VM policies.

- (Preview) Dynamic filter on VM reservation : Placement policies for initial placement can include VM dynamic filter restrictions when the backend feature flag is enabled. A VM reservation will be processed only if the selected VM template's attributes (CPUs, memory size, and storage) match the dynamic filters in the placement policy groups. This applies only to dynamic filters with any of these three attributes.
- -Support for plans with IBM PowerVM environments : For an IBM PowerVM environment, you can now configure and use Optimize on-prem and Hardware refresh plans. Other plans are not currently supported for IBM PowerVM environments.
- -Grace period for delete actions : This release introduces a change to storage policies to avoid unintentional manual deletion of unattached files when the actions are in Manual mode. Any Delete Unattached Files actions that are generated in the grace period between the Generate Delete Action after <your configured number of> Days and the Delete file after <your configured number of> Days settings are created in Recommend mode only, and cannot be executed. After this grace period expires, the action can be executed according to the configured settings. For more information, see Storage settings.
- -Removal of support for VMware Horizon targets : As of version 8.15.5, Turbonomic no longer supports VMware Horizon targets. After you upgrade to version 8.15.5 or later, delete any existing Horizon targets from the Target Configuration page by selecting the target and clicking Delete . Also, it is recommended that you delete horizon and mediation-horizon related settings from the Turbonomic Custom Resource (CR) file. For more information, see (Optional) Enabling and disabling probe components.
- Cloud resource management
- -Disruptiveness and reversibility information for cloud VM scale actions : All scale actions for cloud VMs are disruptive but reversible. These actions require downtime but VMs can be scaled back to their previous tiers or sizes if needed. Scale actions in Action Center now show this information to help you decide whether to execute actions immediately or defer execution to a later time.
- -Support for AWS io2 volumes attached to Relational Database Service (RDS) : Turbonomic now discovers io2 volumes that are attached to RDS instances and recommends scaling these volumes to optimize performance and cost.
- -AWS Enterprise Discount Program (EDP) support for VM actions : Turbonomic now factors in EDP discounts when calculating savings associated with AWS VM actions. For more information, see AWS Billing target and scale actions.

To take advantage of this feature, you need to set up an AWS standard data export (CUR 2.0). If a standard data export is already set up, the following configurations are required:

- Add line\_item\_net\_unblended\_cost to the standard data export. For more information, see Setting up a standard data export (CUR 2.0).
- -Configure EDP discounts in the Price adjustment tab of the Billing and costs page. For more information, see Price adjustment.
- -Guidelines for AWS environments with service control policies (SCPs) : Turbonomic connects to various AWS services and endpoints to discover workloads and pricing data. To successfully connect to these services and endpoints, Turbonomic must not be blocked by SCPs. The documentation now provides guidelines to help you verify the connection and update your SCPs if the connection fails. For more information, see Reviewing your AWS service control policies.
- -Historically informed action generation for Azure workloads : Turbonomic now supports historically informed action generation for the following Azure workloads in both global Azure and Azure Government accounts:
- App service plans
- Cosmos DB containers
- Cosmos DB databases

- Schedule

- -Support for SaaS Reporting in on-prem environments : Starting with version 8.15.4, the SaaS Reporting feature is available for on-prem Turbonomic installations. Previously, this feature was available only for SaaS instances. To begin the enablement process, verify that your company has an active IBM Passport Advantage agreement and then open a case with IBM support. Submit the case with a severity of 2 and provide the following details in the case description:

kubectl exec consul[TAB] -- consul kv get instanceID

Your Turbonomic representative will begin processing enablement requests on March 31, 2025. Version 8.15.4 is now the minimum version for SaaS Reporting in all environment types. For more information, see Enabling SaaS reporting for on-prem instances.

- -SaaS Reporting button enabled by default : Starting with 8.15.6, SaaS Reporting is enabled by default for all Turbonomic users. For on-premises deployments, an information icon appears next to the REPORTS (NEW) button. When users hover over the button, a one-time pop-up provides instructions on how to request provisioning of a SaaS reporting environment. This change is intended to improve user awareness and encourage adoption of the new reporting experience.
- -New sustainability default Reporting Liveboard "Carbon Footprint - Public Cloud" : The new default Reporting Liveboard provides visibility into energy consumption and carbon emissions from public cloud VMs (AWS, Azure and Google Cloud). This Liveboard helps users track their environmental impact while uncovering opportunities to reduce energy usage and optimize workloads efficiently. For more information, see Carbon Footprint - Public Cloud.

- -Turbonomic installation on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) : This release introduces support for installing Turbonomic on an AKS cluster that meets specific requirements. For more information, see Turbonomic installation on an AKS cluster.

This component is now enabled by default and you do not have to manually enable it in your Turbonomic custom resource file. The extractor uses minimal resources until you enable one of the integrations that it supports. For more information about enabling these integrations, see Enabling the Data Exporter and Enabling embedded reporting.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Private preview program]

The Turbonomic private preview program provides an opportunity for customers to deliver feedback on upcoming features before they are publicly available. These previews help Turbonomic build customer feedback into the product much earlier in the process and affirm its customer-centric design focus. To apply to participate in the program, you must first log in to IBM Community with your IBM ID.

Private preview features are not documented. Reach out to your Turbonomic representative to get more information.

For more information about the private preview program and to sign up for preview features, see Turbonomic private previews.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Versioning explanation]

Turbonomic versioning uses V-R-M elements (Version, Release, Modification) in the version number to express the status of a release.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Configuration requirements]

For this release of Turbonomic, you must satisfy the following configuration requirements.


## Compute and storage requirements

The requirements for running a Turbonomic instance depend on the deployment method and the size of the environment you are managing.

Virtual machine image installations of Turbonomic version 8.9.1 or later require at least 1.5 TB for disk storage (that uses Thin provisioning or Thick provisioning), and the /var partition must be at least 340 GB. For more information, see Installing on a Virtual Machine Image.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

Before updating Turbonomic, you must extend the /var partition to at least 340 GB. If the /var partition requirement is not met, your upgrade may fail, new container images may not load properly, and you can run into an ImagePullBackOff issue for some of the images. Before upgrading, be sure that the partition has sufficient disk space. If you need to free up disk space to increase the size of the partition, you can delete old images that are not in use. For details, see Increasing Available Disk Space.

For more information, see Minimum requirements.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Database capacity requirements]

For Turbonomic versions 8.9.0 or later, your historical database must provide certain storage and memory size capacities. For MariaDB or MySQL installations, your database must provide the necessary memory, messaging, and logging capacity.

For its historical database, Turbonomic supports long-term maintenance stable series of MariaDB (the minimum supported version is 10.6) and MySQL 8.0.x. This support includes comprehensive testing and quality control for Turbonomic usage.

For more information, see Configuring a Remote Database.

If you installed Turbonomic as an OVA, and use the included MariaDB for the historic database, you can set the correct capacities by updating your Turbonomic deployment to the latest version. For more information, see Increasing Your Database Capacities.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

If your external database server is multi-tenant, or if your database server does not grant administrative privileges to Turbonomic, then you must continue with this configuration requirement.

Azure database services are multi-tenant. If you deployed an external database on Azure, this configuration requirement applies to you.

If you deployed your database server in a way that grants Turbonomic privileges to create new databases and new users, then the update automatically creates the necessary database. This configuration requirement does not apply to you.

For some Turbonomic updates, the updated version includes new databases on the server. If you are updating to one of these versions, then you must first create the new database and a user account with privileges to access that database. Then, you can update to the latest version of Turbonomic.

For more information, see External DBs and Updates.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Transport Layer Security requirements]

By default, Turbonomic requires Transport Layer Security (TLS) version 1.2 to establish secure communications with targets. Most targets have TLS 1.2 enabled; however, some targets do not enable TLS or they enabled an earlier version. In that case, you see handshake errors when Turbonomic tries to connect with the target service. When you go to the Target Configuration view, you see a Validation Failed status for such targets.

NetApp filers often do not enable TLS and the supported version is TLS 1.0, which causes the NetApp target to fail validation.

If target validation fails because of TLS support, you see validation errors with the following strings:

- No appropriate protocol

Ensure that you enable the latest version of TLS that your target technology supports.

- Certificates do not conform to algorithm constraints

Refer to the documentation for your target technology (such as the NetApp documentation) for instructions to generate a certification key with a length of 1024 or greater on your target server.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > REST API notes]

This section describes issues that result in changes to the REST API. It is a running list of changes that accumulates until the next release of the API Guide. New versions of the guide include these changes. At that time, this list will start with new changes to the API.

Because the API is a full reflection of the Turbonomic product, some changes to the product necessarily cause changes in the API. This can include bug fixes and improvements to the product. For example, new

commodities that you can get for a given entity type may be added, or a bug fix might change the data that is returned by an API request. IBM strives to make these changes backward-compatible whenever possible.

In some instances, changes that are not backward-compatible must be made. In this case, the change is deprecated for a period of time that should be sufficient for you to understand the change and implement an alternative in your scripts.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > REST API changes]

•

Assign and remove user-defined tags on entities and groups

- Use the POST /entities/entity\_Uuid/tags endpoint to assign tags to a specific entity. The existing tags for the entity are not overwritten when invoking the API.
- Use the POST /groups/entity\_Uuid/tags endpoint to assign tags to a specific group. The existing tags for the group are not overwritten when invoking the API.
- Use the DELETE /entities/entity\_Uuid/tags?key=ExampleTagKey endpoint to delete tags of a specified entity. The tags defined in your list are deleted. If no list is provided, then all tags for the entity are deleted.
- Use the DELETE /groups/entity\_Uuid/tags?key=ExampleTagKey endpoint to delete tags of a specified group. The tags defined in your list are deleted. If no list is provided, then all tags for the group are deleted.
- New support for rejecting actions through the Actions API

POST /actions/{action\_uuid} endpoint request now supports rejecting actions. Only actions in a READY state can be rejected. The rejected actions will not be recommended by Turbonomic for the next 7 days.

- The PARKER\_AUTOMATOR role is now available.

The PARKER\_AUTOMATOR role is now supported for POST , GET , and PUT requests to the following user management endpoints:

- -/authorization/oauth2/clients
- -/users
- -/users/ldap

Users with the PARKER\_AUTOMATOR role can park workloads manually or automatically (by attaching parking schedules to workloads), and view all charts and data. However, these users cannot perform the following tasks:

- Manage parking schedules (add, create, or delete schedules)
- Place workloads
- Create policies and templates
- Run plans
- Execute actions
- Pause parking schedule now supports groups

The /parking/enforcementPauses endpoint now supports group IDs for both POST and DELETE requests. You can include either the entityUuids or groupUuids field in the request, and the response will return the corresponding identifier.

- Audit log endpoint is now available

Use the GET /admin/auditlogs endpoint to view audit log data such as login, logout, account management, policy changes, and authorization-related events for Turbonomic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Turbonomic SaaS]

A SaaS server is a Turbonomic instance in a public cloud environment that IBM provisions, maintains, and updates on your behalf. This server can manage the same targets that a customer-hosted Turbonomic instance supports. See the following sections to manage your Turbonomic SaaS deployment:

- 'Managing the SaaS server' on page 57
- 'Managing cloud and cloud-based targets' on page 58
- 'Managing on-prem targets using the secure client' on page 59
- 'Deploying Kubeturbo with the secure client' on page 92

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Turbonomic self-hosted deployment]

You can install Turbonomic as a virtual machine image.

You can get a download of the Turbonomic platform as a:

- VMware Open Virtual Appliance (OVA) 1.0 image
- Microsoft Hyper-V image

You also have the option to install Turbonomic on Kubernetes clusters. Currently, installation on Kubernetes clusters is supported on the Red Hat OpenShift platform, AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). It is possible to install on any upstream compliant Kubernetes, but your Turbonomic representative might not be able to provide support.

Note: Before you install Turbonomic, you need to review the license requirements, networking requirements and compute requirements based on your deployment method.

- Managing Turbonomic SaaS
- Minimum requirements for virtual machine image
- General requirements for Kubernetes
- Requirements for Red Hat OpenShift
- Requirements for AWS EKS
- Requirements for Google GKE
- Requirements for Azure AKS

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Virtual machine image requirements]

The requirements for running a Turbonomic instance depend on the deployment method and the size of the environment you are managing.

Turbonomic keeps a real-time representation of your environment in memory. The greater the number of entities to manage, and the more extensive the relationships between them, the more resources you need for the VM that runs Turbonomic. As the VM requirements increase, so do the requirements for the physical machine that hosts the VM.

The requirements that are listed for each deployment method are recommendations that you should keep in mind as you plan your Turbonomic deployment. After deploying Turbonomic, if you need to change memory capacity, CPU capacity, or both for the VM, you can shut it down, make changes, and then power it up again to use the new capacity.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

The machine that hosts the Turbonomic platform must support the SSE4.2 instruction set. Support for this instruction set was introduced at different times for different chip manufacturers:

- Intel: November 2008
- AMD: October 2011

The machine that hosts Turbonomic should be newer than these dates. On a Linux system, you can run the following command to check for this support:

cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep sse4

For more information, see the glossary entry at http://www.cpu-world.com/Glossary/S/SSE4.html.

Usually you can run Turbonomic on a host that meets the following minimum requirements:

| Supported VMImage technology   | Supported VMImage technology                              | Storage requirements                                                                                                 | Memory                                                                                                                                               | CPUs     |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|
| VMware Microso ft              | vCenter versions 7.0 and 8.0 Hyper-V Server 2012 R2 later | 1.75 TB or greater (using Thin provisioning or Thick provisioning) Note: The /var partition must be at least 340 GB. | • Default: 160 GB • For 10,000 VMs or less, 96 GB Note: If you plan to install a VM with 96 GB of memory, you must modify the default for VM memory. | 12 vCPUs |

Turbonomic provides a VM image (an OVA or VHD file) which is preconfigured with two hard disk drives. A minimum of 1.80 TB is necessary to ensure that the drives have the proper amount of space for storage.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Network]

The operator creates an NGINX LoadBalancer service by default, which uses an IP address or a load balancing service (external or internal), depending on the annotation.

Public IP and elastic load balancing are the default load balancers in the public cloud. However, it is recommended that you leverage one of the load balancers that is offered by the cloud provider, such as Network Load Balancer (NLB) or Application Load Balancer (ALB), and then configure the service annotations available for the chosen load balancer in the Turbonomic Custom Resource.

Since NGINX is deployed as a proxy service, you must edit the Custom Resource YAML to include NGINX attributes. Additionally, you can choose to have Turbonomic create a route in front of NGINX or you can manually create the route.

For more information, see NGINX Service Configuration Options and Platform Provided Ingress and Routes.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Container image repository]

Turbonomic supports public and private container image repositories. By default, the Turbonomic installation uses the public IBM Container Registry ( icr.io ).

To connect to icr.io , your environment must have direct access to the Internet or indirect access through a proxy server. If your environment is behind a firewall, make sure that you have full access to the IBM Container Registry services that deliver the Turbonomic components. You need to add https:// *.icr.io host address to your allowed firewall rules.

You can configure the installation to pull from a private repository and use pull secrets. For more information, see this topic.

For Red Hat OpenShift installations, if you are air-gapped or running a disconnected cluster and still want to use OperatorHub, see additional information in the Red Hat OpenShift documentation.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Storage]

The Turbonomic platform leverages persistent volumes (PVs) to store logs, certificates, and tokens. The platform uses Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) to create PVs from the cluster's default storage class, or a Security Context that is specified in the Turbonomic Custom Resource.

Recommendations and best practices:

- Use block storage for the PVs used by Turbonomic.
- Volume backup strategy is important. The PVs associated with the api , api-certs , auth , topologyprocessor , and consul-data PVCs should be backed up to ensure recovery in case of server loss. If you are running a containerized database for Turbonomic, back up db-data and datatimescaledb-0 .
- The following Storage Class properties are required:
- To support pods with multiple PVs, especially where your nodes are spread across multiple availability zones or regions, set the binding to be volumeBindingMode = WaitForFirstConsumer .
- Ensure recovery by setting the reclaimPolicy option of Retain .
- Ideally, also use a storage provisioner that allows for volume expansion ( allowVolumeExpansion ).

For PVC details and total storage required, see this topic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Resource recommendations for Kubernetes]

The amount of resources that you need to run Turbonomic is related to the complexity and type of entities that it manages. Entities include objects such as virtual machines, containers, pods, or cloud accounts. Turbonomic takes advantages of containers to scale the platform accordingly.

The following table provides a guideline to the cluster resources that you need to support the entities that you expect to manage in a single Turbonomic instance.

| Size   | Entity scale                                   | Minimum size per node   | Number of nodes   | Estimated total memory consumption (GB)   | Estimated total CPU consumption (Cores)   |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Small  | Up to 1,000 VMs 5,000 to 80,000 entities       | 2 CPUs * 16 GB          | At least 3        | 8 to 42                                   | 3 to 6                                    |
| Medium | 1,000 to 16,000 VMs 80,000 to 200,000 entities | 3 CPUs * 32 GB          | At least 3        | 32 to 91                                  | 4 to 9                                    |
| Large  | 16,000 to 40,000 VMs                           | 4 CPUs * 64 GB          | At least 4        | 50 to 110                                 | 7 to 16                                   |

| Size        | Entity scale                                     | Minimum size per node   | Number of nodes   | Estimated total memory consumption (GB)   | Estimated total CPU consumption (Cores)   |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
|             | 200,000 to 1.5 million entities                  |                         |                   |                                           |                                           |
| Extra large | 40,000 to 180,000 VMs Up to 2.1 million entities | 4 CPUs * 96 GB          | At least 5        | 100 to 209                                | 10 to 20                                  |

Points to consider:

- For large or extra large deployments of , or if you need more then one instance, contact your Turbonomic representative for guidance and assistance.
- Turbonomic creates persistent volumes (PVs) based on dynamic storage provisioning. For more information, see this Storage class requirements.
- The total amount of memory and CPUs required depends on the number and type of enabled mediation components and configured targets. Each target type spins up its own pod.
- Turbonomic supports namespaces with resource quotas. Contact your Turbonomic representative for help in configuring a quota.
- For installations in the public cloud, do not use spot instances in the cluster where you install Turbonomic. Spot instances can be taken down at any time, which can then result in loss of access to Turbonomic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Option 1: NGINX as a proxy and 'bring your own' ingress/route]

You can configure NGINX as a ClusterIP type service, which allows you to use your own ingress/route while maintaining the Turbonomic internal routing rules and leverage NGINX as a proxy. This is required to leverage reporting on your Turbonomic instance with your own ingress/route. You will use the parameter nginxIsPrimaryIngress set to false .

```
kind: XL metadata: name: xl-releasespec: nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false #use openshiftingress and nginxingress if you would like Turbo to create a single route that will point to the nginx service #openshiftingress: #  enabled: true #nginxingress: #  enabled: true
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Option 2: NGINX as a LoadBalancer service type and customized annotations]

Turbonomic does not deploy an ingress controller. It deploys NGINX as a Kubernetes service, which can create a cloud provider load balancer. This load balancer has a type of external or can be used as an internal clusterIP service type that sits behind a customer/platform provided ingress.

It is assumed that you understand the following concepts:

- The types of load balancers that are available to you based on your cloud or infrastructure provider
- All service annotations that are available to you and which annotations are required for your environment

To modify the NGINX load balancer type service to use an internal IP address on your load balancer, use the required annotation according to your Kubernetes platform and version. Use an annotation that is applicable for your environment.

In the Turbonomic Custom Resource, you can specify the proper annotations that you determined are required for the load balancer for your NGINX service.

```
global: ingress: annotations: #provide the correct annotations based on the LB you want and the properties you want.
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > NGINX as proxy and 'bring your own' ingress or route]

You can configure nginx as a ClusterIP type service, allowing you to use your own ingress or route, and still maintain the Turbonomic internal routing rules and leverage nginx as a proxy. This is required to leverage embedded reporting on your Turbonomic instance.

1. Open the CR file for editing.

The location of the file depends on the type of Turbonomic installation that you are configuring.

- VM Image installation of Turbonomic

Log in to an SSH terminal session of your Turbonomic instance as the System Administrator that you set up when you installed Turbonomic.

```
/opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

- Turbonomic on a Kubernetes node or node cluster
2. Modify the CR file to set the nginxIsPrimaryIngress parameter to false .
3. Apply the changes that you made to the CR file.

```
deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

```
kind: XL metadata: name: xl-release spec: global: tag: 8.16.5 nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false #use the following parameters if you would like Turbonomic to create a single OCP route that will point to the nginx service #openshiftingress: #  enabled: true #nginxingress: #  enabled: true
```

For example, run the following command for VM image installations:

```
kubectl apply -f \ /opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Red Hat OpenShift routes and Turbonomic]

The following configuration deploys nginx as a proxy, and creates a single route that points to the nginx proxy:

```
kind: XL metadata: name: xl-release spec: global: tag: 8.16.5 nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false nginxingress: enabled: true openshiftingress: enabled: true
```

<!-- image -->

The name of the default route created will be nginx . To identify the hostname that you will use for your Turbonomic UI URL, while in the Turbonomic platform Project go to Networking > Routes and find the nginx route. The location for the route nginx is the Turbonomic UI URL.

Examples of the default location that is created include nginxyourNamespaceName.apps.yourOCPDomain .

This method creates a single route using a basic configuration with tls.termination: edge; tls.insecure, EdgeTerminationPolicy: Redirect, and using either the default ingress domain or one you define. Multiple routes are no longer created.

Set up the nginx service as a ClusterIP type, and want to create your own Route, you will first set up the Turbonomic CR.

```
kind: XL metadata: name: xl-release spec: global: tag: 8.16.5 nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false

Create a single Route manually with the following properties:
