[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Pulling from a private repository]

To use your own private repository, you need to pull and stage Turbonomic images, which are located in the following repositories based on the deployment method. The components are the same regardless of the deployment method.

| Deployment method             | Default repositories                                                                |
|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Red Hat OpenShift OperatorHub | icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic icr.io/cpopen registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/ubi- minimal |
| Direct deployment             | icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic icr.io/cpopen                                              |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Modifying the Turbonomic custom resource]

After the images are pulled in to your private registry, update the registry and repository location of the Turbonomic server container images in the custom resource yaml. Also update the Operator deployment yaml to pull from the registry.

Modify these values for your environment:

```
global: repository: <yourRegistry> / <yourRepository> _# uncomment line below if using RedHat Container Catalog, and specify `registry.connect.redhat.com/turbonomic` as the `repository`_ _# when deploying from the OCP Operator Hub the `repository` and `customImageNames` will be preconfigured for you_ # customImageNames: false _# for pull credentials, registry parameter is required and the value can be the same as repository_ _# uncomment what you need below if you need to specify pull credentials. Note this will be used for all images._ # registry: <yourRegistry> / <yourRepository> # imageUsername: turbouser # imagePassword: turbopassword # imagePullSecret: <yourSecret> tag: 8.16.5
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

If you are running the t8c-operator before version 42, you must define the registry and repository as shown in the following example:

```
global: registry: <yourRegistry> # imageUsername: turbouser # imagePassword: turbopassword # imagePullSecret: <yourSecret> repository: <yourRepository> tag:8.16.5
```

If you require credentials to access your registry, you can specify the username and password credentials as shown in the following example:

```
global: repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic registry: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic imageUsername: turbouser imagePassword: turbopassword # imagePullSecret: <yourSecret> tag: 8.16.5
```

- The registry parameter is required in the CR to use the imageUsername / imagePassword or imagePullSecret parameters.

- The customImageNames parameter must be set to false when working with Red Hat Operators and the Red Hat Container Catalog. You must also specify registry.connect.redhat.com/ turbonomic for both registry and repository .

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

When you deploy from the Red Hat OpenShift Operator Hub, these values are preset for you.

- This method creates a Kubernetes Secret of type docker-registry with the default name of turbocred . It then applies the pullSecret parameter to the Turbonomic component deployments.

Next, update the image: value in the Operator deployment yaml to pull from the repository.

```
containers: - name: t8c-operator image: <yourRegistry> / <yourRepo> /t8c-operator:42.84
```

If required, update the Turbonomic Operator to use the pull credentials. You can specify the image pull Secret in the Operator deployment yaml, or add this Secret to the t8c-operator service account.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > 2. Link the Secret to the service account.]

For the Operator, configure the t8c-operator service account for the image pull Secret. For more information, see the Kubernetes documentation.

In Red Hat OpenShift, run the oc secrets link command:

```
oc secrets link t8c-operator yourSecret -- for=pull
```


## Note:

To use this method for the Turbonomic pods, associate the Secret to the default service account.

```
oc secrets link default yourSecret --for=pull
```

For more information, see the Kubernetes documentation.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Storage class requirements]

A persistent volume (PV) is a piece of storage in the Kubernetes cluster, while a persistent volume claim (PVC) is a request for storage. The Turbonomic platform uses persistent volumes to store logs, certificates, tokens, and some data for some of the services. It also dynamically provisions storage by using persistent volume claims to create PVs from the cluster's default storage class.

The following list outlines the recommended properties for a storage class. Follow the instructions for the storage provisioner that you are using.

- Use a dynamic storage provisioner; Turbonomic creates the PVC.
- Use a storage class that provides Block storage.
- Set Volume Expansion to be True .
- Set Reclaim Policy to Retain .
- Set Volume Binding Mode to WaitForFirstConsumer .
- Encryption is supported.
- Consider whether you want to use storage that is multi-zoned, but the cost will likely be more.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Best Practices]

- The Turbonomic platform relies on data that is stored in PVs that are important to retain target, licensing, and historical data association. Minimally you can use the reclaimPolicy option of Retain in the storage class. Back up the PVs associated with the following PVCs to aid in recovery if there is a loss of the server: api, api-certs, auth, and consul-data .
- Volume backup strategy is important. If you are running a containerized DB for Turbonomic, the embedded reporting feature, or both, include these PVs to preserve: db-data and datatimescaledb-0 .
- Use a storage class that allows for volume expansion ( allowVolumeExpansion ) for the DB PVs.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Non-default storage class]

The Turbonomic deployment uses the cluster's default storage class if one is defined. If you want to use a different storage class, specify the name of the storage class in the Turbonomic CR and apply the change.

1. Open the CR file for editing.

The location of the file depends on the type of Turbonomic installation that you are configuring.

- VM Image installation of Turbonomic

Log in to an SSH terminal session of your Turbonomic instance as the System Administrator that you set up when you installed Turbonomic.

/opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

- Turbonomic on a Kubernetes node or node cluster

deploy/crds/charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml

2. Modify the CR file to include the storage class.
3. Apply the changes that you made to the CR file.

```
global: repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic >
```

```
tag: 8.16.5 storageClassName: < yourStorageClass externalIP: 10.97.96.3 pullPolicy: Always
```

For example, run the following command for VM image installations:

```
kubectl apply -f \ /opt/turbonomic/kubernetes/operator/deploy/crds/charts_v1alpha1_xl_cr.yaml
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > General requirements for persistent volumes]

The following table describes the PVC resources and default configurations.

| Component          | Persistent volume claim   |   Size in Gi (default) | Notes                                                                        |
|--------------------|---------------------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| api                | api                       |                      1 |                                                                              |
| api                | api-certs                 |                      1 |                                                                              |
| auth               | auth                      |                      1 |                                                                              |
| consul             | consul-data               |                      1 |                                                                              |
| db                 | db-data                   |                    500 | This component is not required when you use an external DB server or service |
| kafka              | kafka-log                 |                     50 |                                                                              |
| prometheus         | prometheus-server         |                      8 |                                                                              |
| redis(suspend)     | redis-data-redis-master-0 |                      4 | This component is required for the Parking feature.                          |
| rsyslog            | rsyslog-auditlogdata      |                     30 |                                                                              |
| rsyslog            | rsyslog-syslogdata        |                     30 |                                                                              |
| topology-processor | topology-processor        |                      3 |                                                                              |
| zookeeper          | zookeeper-data            |                      3 |                                                                              |
| timescaledb        | data-timescaledb-0        |                    125 | This component is required if embedded reporting is enabled.                 |

| Component   | Persistent volume claim   | Size in Gi (default)   | Notes                                                                     |
|-------------|---------------------------|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|             |                           |                        | Specify a new value for spec: postgresql: persistence: size: < value > Gi |

If you want to deploy with a different volume size, specify the volume in the Custom Resource. Combine these settings with any other properties specified. See the following example for db where the PVC size and Mem Limits are modified.

```
db: resources: limits: memory: 16Gi persistence: size: 500Gi
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Assumptions]

This topic assumes the following:

- You are familiar with AWS EKS clusters and associated resources, such as the EBS CSI driver and EKS load balancers. You know how to deploy and manage these clusters and resources, and troubleshoot any issues that are not related to your Turbonomic installation.
- The AWS EKS cluster for your Turbonomic installation has been created and is running.


## General requirements

To install Turbonomic, your environment must meet certain requirements. Before proceeding, be sure to review the requirements outlined in Kubernetes installation general requirements.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > AWS EKS cluster]

The AWS EKS cluster that you use for your Turbonomic installation must meet the following requirements:

| Item                                    | Requirements                                                                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cluster service role                    | Your EKS cluster must be assigned an IAM role that includes the following policies: • AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy • AmazonEKSServicePolicy • AdministratorAccess |
| Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnets | Use the default or create a new one.                                                                                                                          |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > AWS EKS cluster nodes]

The nodes in the AWS EKS cluster must meet the following requirements:

| Item                            | Requirements                                                                                                                                                         |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Amazon Machine Image (AMI) type | Turbonomic recommends nodes with the Managed Linux node type, which runs Amazon Linux applications on Amazon EC2 instances.                                          |
| Node IAM role                   | The nodes must be assigned an IAM role that includes the following policies: • AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy • AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly • AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy |

| Item                                           | Requirements                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Instance type                                  | • The instance type must have sufficient resources for Turbonomic to manage your environment. For guidance on the required resources based on the size of your environment, see this topic. • Do not use spot instances. Spot instances can be taken down at any time, which can then result in loss of access to Turbonomic. • Instance types running ARM-based processors (for example, AWS Graviton) are not supported. • Instance types running AWS Fargate are not recommended . |
| Available storage for persistent volumes (PVs) | At least 150 GB is required to support all PVs. For more information, see 'General requirements for persistent volumes' on page 48.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Node group scaling configuration               | The cluster to which you install Turbonomic must have at least three worker nodes. For guidance on the number of nodes to create based on the size of your environment, see this topic.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

Security context does not need to be annotated. You can give Turbonomic the name of a specific security context to use.

The following example shows a YAML resource that meets the requirements.

```
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata: name: gp3-new provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com parameters: fsType: ext4 type: gp3
```

```
reclaimPolicy: Retain volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer allowVolumeExpansion: true
```

For more information, see this topic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > GKE cluster]

The GKE cluster that you use for your Turbonomic installation must meet the following requirements:

| Item              | Requirements                                                                                                                         |
|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cluster type      | Create a standard cluster. Do not create an Autopilot cluster as this configuration can be detrimental to performance of Turbonomic. |
| Location type     | For more information, see 'Persistent volumes in public cloud' on page 49.                                                           |
| Node pool scaling | For guidance on the number of nodes to create based on the size of your environment, see                                             |

| Item                                           | Requirements                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|                                                | 'Resource recommendations for Kubernetes' on page 40.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Cluster autoscaler                             | Enable the cluster autoscaler to automatically create or delete nodes based on your workload needs. For more information, see Google Cloud documentation.                                                                                                          |
| Available storage for persistent volumes (PVs) | At least 150 GB of storage is required to support all the PVs for your Turbonomic installation. You might require additional storage depending on your specific configuration. For more information, see 'General requirements for persistent volumes' on page 48. |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

pd-ssd disk type offers more input output operations per second (IOPS), lower latency, and is suitable for high-performance databases. For more information about disk types, see Google Cloud documentation.

If you are using a containerized database, it is recommended to choose pd-ssd . For non-containerized database, the pd-balanced disk type is sufficient.

The following example shows a YAML resource that meets the requirements.

```
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata: name: standard-rwo-retain annotations: components.gke.io/layer: addon labels: addonmanager.kubernetes.io/mode: EnsureExists k8s-app: gcp-compute-persistent-disk-csi-driver parameters: type: pd-ssd provisioner: pd.csi.storage.gke.io reclaimPolicy: Retain volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer allowVolumeExpansion: true
```

For more information, see Storage class requirements.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > AKS cluster]

The AKS cluster that you use for your Turbonomic installation must meet the following requirements:

| Item                                           | Requirements                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Cluster type                                   | Create a Kubernetes cluster cluster within Kubernetes services.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Cluster preset configuration                   | Do not use Dev/Test and Production Economy . Select configuration presets based on your requirements. For more information about configuration presets, see Azure documentation.                                                                                                   |
| Region                                         | Select a region, such as East US 2 . Select Availability zones and AKS pricing tier as per requirements.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Node pool                                      | In Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), a node pool is a group of Kubernetes nodes (Azure VMs) with the same configuration, allowing you to manage and scale your cluster's compute resources effectively. For more information about Node pool configuration, see Azure documentation. |
| DNS name prefix                                | Under Networking tab, enter a name for DNS prefix.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Network policy                                 | Select None for network policy. This option allows all ingress and egress traffic to the pods.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Available storage for persistent volumes (PVs) | At least 150 GB of storage is required to support all the PVs for your Turbonomic installation. You might require additional storage depending on your specific configuration. For more information, see 'General requirements for persistent volumes' on page 48.                 |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Custom storage class]

The custom storage class must meet the following requirements.

| Item           | Requirements                  |
|----------------|-------------------------------|
| Binding mode   | Set to WaitForFirstConsumer . |
| Reclaim policy | Set to Retain .               |

| Item             | Requirements   |
|------------------|----------------|
| Volume expansion | Set to true .  |

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Note:]

Premium\_LRS disk type offers more input output operations per second (IOPS) and lower latency, and is therefore suitable for high-performance databases. For more information about storage classes, see Storage classes.

If you are using a containerized database, it is recommended to choose Premium\_LRS . For noncontainerized database, the StandardSSD\_LRS disk type is sufficient.

The following example shows a YAML resource that meets the requirements.

```
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata: name: managed-csi-retain provisioner: disk.csi.azure.com parameters: skuName: StandardSSD_LRS reclaimPolicy: Retain volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer allowVolumeExpansion: true
```

For more information, see Storage class requirements.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Terminology]

- SaaS server

A SaaS server is a Turbonomic instance in a public cloud environment that IBM provisions, maintains, and updates on your behalf. This server can manage the same targets that a customer-hosted Turbonomic instance supports.

For more information, see this topic.

- Secure client (secure connector for hybrid support)

A secure client, also known as the secure connector for hybrid support, is an agent that you install in your on-prem environment so that a SaaS server can manage on-prem targets, such as VMware vCenter and Red Hat OpenShift.

The secure client automatically updates each time your Turbonomic representative updates your SaaS server to a new version. The update process keeps the version of the secure client components (probes and tunnel) in sync with the server. If the secure client is unable to update for some reason, it attempts to update periodically until it succeeds.

For more information on the secure client installation methods, see this topic.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Requesting a SaaS server]

Contact your Turbonomic representative to request access to a SaaS server.

If you want to try the product, a 30-day trial is available from the IBM website or AWS marketplace. When the product is ready to use, log in to the user interface and review the following items:

- The banner on the page, which indicates how long you have left in your trial. It also provides options to check pricing and initiate a purchase.
- Links to a product tour and video

Take a product tour or watch a video to learn more about Turbonomic and the many benefits that it offers.

- Getting started pages

These pages are intended to help you set up and use the product in three easy steps.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Logging in to the SaaS server]

Before you can log in to your SaaS server, your enterprise must have a valid Turbonomic account. Contact your Turbonomic representative to get the following information for your account:

- SaaS server address
- Login credentials (user name and password)
1. Open a browser window and specify the SaaS server address in the address bar.
2. Log in using the user name and password for your account.

After you log in, the Home page displays. This page is your starting point for sessions with the Turbonomic platform. Bookmark the URL for this page for future use.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Requirements]

- TLS over TCP :

The proxy server must support TLS over TCP on port 443, which is the default port for TLS traffic. The secure client does not support configured proxies or proxy servers that support HTTP only. Transparent proxies (implicit proxies) that support TLS over TCP are supported.

- TLS passthrough :

The proxy server must not terminate the TLS session originating from the secure client. This is sometimes called TLS passthrough mode as opposed to the re-encrypt mode.

With mTLS passthrough, encrypted traffic from the secure clients is passed on to the SaaS server without undergoing decryption in the proxy server. As the data packets are only decrypted on the SaaS server, the encrypted traffic is secure from the malicious attacks.

- Server name indication :

The proxy server must support server name indication (SNI).

SNI is an extension of the TLS protocol that reads the domain name of the SaaS server during the TLS handshake. This enables the proxy server to direct the data to the SaaS server.

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Client Network Tokens]

Firewall requirements:

If a secure client is behind a firewall, you must first ensure it can make outbound requests to the following external fully qualified domain

name/port combinations:

- claims-turbonomic.apps.acme.com:443 - skupper-edge-turbonomic.apps.acme.com:443

- skupper-inter-router-turbonomic.apps.acme.com:443

If you do not have the URL or login credentials of your SaaS server, contact your Turbonomic representative.

SaaS server endpoints must resemble the following list:

```
1. claims-turbonomic.apps.acme.com 2. skupper-edge-turbonomic.apps.acme.com 3. skupper-inter-router-turbonomic.apps.acme.com
```

[Section: IBMTurbonomic_8.16.5 > Example proxy server configuration]

A sample HAProxy configuration file is provided to illustrate the two requirements:

```

## Use SNI to send the request to the appropriate backend frontend public_ssl bind :443 tcp-request inspect-delay 5s tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 } use_backend be_claims if { req.ssl_sni -i claims-turbonomic.apps.acme.com } use_backend be_skupper-edge if { req.ssl_sni -i skupper-edge-turbonomic.apps.acme.com } use_backend be_skupper-inter-router if { req.ssl_sni -i skupper-inter-routerturbonomic.apps.acme.com } # TLS passthrough for claims route backend be_claims balance source hash-type consistent timeout check 5000ms server skupper-claims claims-turbonomic.apps.acme.com:443 weight 1 check # TLS passthrough for skupper-edge route backend be_skupper-edge balance source hash-type consistent timeout check 5000ms server skupper-router skupper-edge-turbonomic.apps.acme.com:443 weight 1 check # TLS passthrough for skupper-inter-router route backend be_skupper-inter-router balance source hash-type consistent
```

- Minimum requirements

The requirements for running a Turbonomic instance depend on the size of the environment you are managing. Turbonomic keeps a real-time representation of your environment in memory. A large environment and extensive relationships between entities in the environment require more resources for the VM that runs Turbonomic and the VM's host.

Refer to the following requirements as you plan your Turbonomic deployment. After the deployment, if you find that you need to change the VM's memory capacity, CPU capacity, or both, you can power off the VM, make changes, and then power it on again to use the new capacity.

| Environment size               |   Recommended memory (GB) |   Recommended vCPUs (cores) |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Small 0-5k entities            |                        32 |                           8 |
| Medium 5k-80k entities         |                        64 |                          16 |
| Large 80k-200k entities        |                       128 |                          32 |
| Extra Large 200k-1.5M entities |                       192 |                          48 |

- Network requirements

Secure clients have the following network requirements:

- Proxy environments are only supported in certain conditions. For more information, see 'Configuring a proxy server for the secure client' on page 61.
- SSL inspection on the customer firewall is not supported.
- During installation and update, Docker images are downloaded from the icr.io image repository. The images themselves exist on sub-domains of icr.io , for example dd2.icr.io , but these sub-domain names may change. If a firewall exists between the OVA and the internet, connections to icr.io and its sub-domains (that is, *.icr.io ) must be allowed so that the OVA can download the images.

When you install secure client using 'Installing the secure client without OLM and with a private image registry' on page 68 method, then no connection from the OVA to icr.io is required as the images are obtained from the private registry.

- Firewall ports

If the secure client is behind a firewall, ensure that all nodes in the cluster can make outbound requests to several external fully qualified domain name and port combinations that are exposed on your SaaS environment. To view the list of fully qualified domain name and port combinations, open the Turbonomic user interface, navigate to Settings > Secure Client Management , and then click the Server Details tab.

If you do not see the Secure Client Management option in the Settings page or if the Server Details tab is empty, log a support ticket and request that Secure Client Management be enabled in your SaaS server.

Nothing needs to be changed on the VM created from the OVA. Any firewall changes are specific to your own environment.

- Connection verification

You can run /opt/local/bin/check\_connection.sh command to verify that the required DNS name and port combinations are accessible from the secure client environment. The four DNS names must resolve to the same IP address so it is only necessary to run the command for one of the DNS named listed. For example, to verify the connection to claims-acme.turbonomic.io at port 443, run the following command:

```
/opt/local/bin/check_connection.sh --ip claims-acme.turbonomic.io --port 443
```

The output is similar to the following example:

```
Checking connectivity to claims-acme.turbonomic.io :443... The request to claims-acme.turbonomic.io :443 was successful
```

- Access to IBM Container Registry

For the self-upgrading probe capability to work, the client environment must be able to pull new images from the IBM Container Registry, if not using a private registry.

To allow the secure client to update automatically, add the following addresses to the allowlist:

```
https://icr.io https://*.icr.io
```

For instructions on installing the image as a standalone platform that manages both on-prem and cloud targets, see OVA: Installing the vCenter image for on-prem environments.

1. Download the Turbonomic installation package.

The email you received from IBM includes links to the Turbonomic download pages. You can get the installation package from there.

The installation package includes the turbonomic\_t8c-<version> -<XXXXXXXXXXXXXX> .ova file where <version> is the Turbonomic version number and <XXXXXXXXXXXXXX> is the timestamp.

The OVA file deploys as a VM with the Turbonomic components already installed.

2. Import the OVA file into your datacenter.

Use the vCenter Server client to import the OVA into your environment.

3. Deploy the Turbonomic VM.

Configure the VM that was deployed from the OVA file. Ensure that the physical machine hosting the VM meets the minimum requirements.

4. Open the remote console.

For the Turbonomic VM that you just deployed:

- a. Choose the Summary tab.
- b. Click Launch Remote Console .
5. Set up the Turbonomic System Administrator account.
- a. In the remote console, log in with the following default credentials:
- Username: turbo

Do not use the account name, root .

- Password: vmturbo

Then, you will be prompted to enter a new password.

- b. Enter your new password.

The new password must comply with the strong password policy (a mixture of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and a symbol). Only you will know this new password.

6. Update the root password.

The platform uses the root account for certain processes, such as rolling up log messages in /var/log/messages . To ensure the account credentials are current, you must change the password:

- a. Open a SuperUser session.
- In the remote console, enter su -
- At the password prompt, enter the default password: vmturbo

After you install the OVA image, install and configure the secure client. By default, automatic updates are enabled to keep the secure client components (probes and tunnel) in sync with the server.

There are several ways to install the secure client.

| Installation method                                                                        | Details                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| (Recommended) Secure client installation with Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM)             | The secure client operator and probes are updated automatically.                                                                                                                                                              |
| (Not recommended) Secure client installation without OLM                                   | The secure client operator is not updated automatically but probes are updated automatically.                                                                                                                                 |
| (Not recommended) Secure client installation without OLM and with a private image registry | The secure client operator is not updated automatically and all images must be available in the private image registry before installation or upgrade. Probes are updated automatically if the relevant images are available. |

The lifespan of a token is the amount of time before the token expires. An expired token cannot be used to add a client.

An example where the same token can be used for multiple clients is Kubeturbo. If there are many Kubeturbo agents to be connected, it may be convenient to generate one token and apply the same token to each Kubeturbo agent. In this case, increase the claim limit to match the number of Kubeturbo agents to be added and increase the lifespan to allow enough time for the token to be applied to all agents.

- e. Click Create .

Download the token value or copy the token to the clipboard.

2. Apply the token to the secure client.
- a. Open an SSH terminal session on your secure client instance.
- b. Run the tokenExchange.sh script, specifying the Kubernetes namespace if required. This defaults to turbonomic if omitted.
- c. When prompted, paste the entire token that you obtained from the SaaS server.

```
/opt/local/bin/tokenExchange.sh -n turbonomic
```

{ "kind": "Secret",
```

- Firewall ports

If the secure client is behind a firewall, ensure that all nodes in the cluster can make outbound requests to several external fully qualified domain name and port combinations that are exposed on your SaaS environment. To view the list of fully qualified domain name and port combinations, open the Turbonomic user interface, navigate to Settings > Secure Client Management , and then click the Server Details tab.

If you do not see the Secure Client Management option in the Settings page or if the Server Details tab is empty, log a support ticket and request that Secure Client Management be enabled in your SaaS server.

- Access to IBM Container Registry

For the self-upgrading probe capability to work, the client environment must be able to pull new images from the IBM Container Registry, if not using a private registry.

Add the following address to the allowlist for all nodes of the cluster:

```
https://icr.io https://*.icr.io
```

The claim limit of a token is the number of clients that can be added by using the same token. If you need to connect multiple clients with the same token, increase the claim limit to match the number of clients to be added.

Lifespan

The lifespan of a token is the amount of time before the token expires. An expired token cannot be used to add a client.

An example where the same token can be used for multiple clients is Kubeturbo. If there are many Kubeturbo agents to be connected, it may be convenient to generate one token and apply the same token to each Kubeturbo agent. In this case, increase the claim limit to match the number of Kubeturbo agents to be added and increase the lifespan to allow enough time for the token to be applied to all agents.

- e. Click Create .

Download the token value or copy the token to the clipboard.

2. Apply the token to the secure client.

After you create the token, it must be applied as a Kubernetes Secret within the same Red Hat OpenShift project as your secure client.

- a. On the Red Hat OpenShift UI, navigate to Workloads > Secrets .
- b. Click Create > From YAML , which is displayed on the upper-right side of the Secrets window.
- c. Replace the existing content with the token you generated in the UI and click Create .

For reference, the JSON output should be similar to the following example:

```
{ "apiVersion": "v1", "data": { "ca.crt": " <base64 encoded certificate> ", "password": " <base64 encoded password> "
```

```
}, "kind": "Secret", "metadata": { "annotations": { "skupper.io/generated-by": "aa7e96fe-bbcb-48b2-b2ce-a6a87b12a53d", "skupper.io/site-version": "1.2.4", "skupper.io/url": " <URL of SaaS instance used for token exchange> " }, "labels": { "skupper.io/type": "token-claim" }, "name": "5c3155c7-5a04-11ed-a12e-92430b25f882" } }
```

3. Verify that the connection was established.

If the connection was successful, the remote-nginx-tunnel and remote-rsylog services will be visible on the Services page.

- a. Navigate to Networking > Services .
- b. In the Filter by name box, enter remote .
- c. Review to ensure the remote-nginx-tunnel and remote-rsylog services are visible.

- Firewall ports

If the secure client is behind a firewall, ensure that all nodes in the cluster can make outbound requests to several external fully qualified domain name and port combinations that are exposed on your SaaS environment. To view the list of fully qualified domain name and port combinations, open the Turbonomic user interface, navigate to Settings > Secure Client Management , and then click the Server Details tab.

If you do not see the Secure Client Management option in the Settings page or if the Server Details tab is empty, log a support ticket and request that Secure Client Management be enabled in your SaaS server.

- Access to IBM Container Registry

For the self-upgrading probe capability to work, the client environment must be able to pull new images from the IBM Container Registry, if not using a private registry.

Add the following address to the allowlist for all nodes of the cluster:

```
https://icr.io https://*.icr.io
```

Note: This installation method is recommended.

1. Open an SSH terminal session.
2. Create a namespace. The rest of the client installation steps are done in this namespace.

kubectl create namespace <my-namespace>

Switch to the new namespace.

```
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace <my-namespace>
```

3. Install the Operator Lifecycle Manager (OLM). The supported release version for OLM is v0.23.1.

```
curl -L https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-lifecycle-manager/releases/download/ v0.23.1/install.sh -o install.sh chmod +x install.sh
```

Run the install script to create all of the necessary k8s resources.

```
./install.sh v0.23.1
```

The output is similar to the following example:

```
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/catalogsources.operators.coreos.com created customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/clusterserviceversions.operators.coreos.com
```

```
created customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/installplans.operators.coreos.com created ... Package server phase: Installing Package server phase: Succeeded Waiting for deployment "packageserver" rollout to finish: 1 of 2 updated replicas are available... deployment "packageserver" successfully rolled out
```

Verify that the OLM installed correctly.

```
kubectl get csv -n olm
```

The output is similar to the following example:

```
NAME            DISPLAY          VERSION   REPLACES   PHASE packageserver   Package Server   0.23.1               Succeeded
```

4. Install the secure client operator.

To install the secure client operator, you must create yaml files for three entities: CatalogSource , OperatorGroup , and Subscription .

- a. Create a new file called catalogSource.yaml and add the following content:

```
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
```

```
kind: CatalogSource metadata: name: t8c-client-operator-catalog namespace: olm spec: grpcPodConfig: securityContextConfig: restricted displayName: Turbonomic Client Operator image: icr.io/cpopen/t8c-client-operator-catalog publisher: Turbonomic.com sourceType: grpc updateStrategy: registryPoll: interval: 60m
```

Apply the file content.

kubectl apply -f catalogSource.yaml

- b. Create a new file called operatorGroup.yaml and add the following content:

```
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1
```

```
kind: OperatorGroup metadata: name: turbonomic-operators spec: targetNamespaces: -<my-namespace>
```

Note: This installation method is not recommended.

1. Ensure that all of the required images are available in the private image registry. For example, to install the 8.16.5 version of the secure client, the following images are required:
- icr.io/cpopen/t8c-client-operator:1.4.1
- icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/kube-state-metrics:v2.14.0
- icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/tsc-site-resources:8.16.5
- icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/rsyslog-courier:8.16.5
- icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/skupper-site-controller:8.16.5

```
· icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/skupper-router:8.16.5 · icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/skupper-config-sync:8.16.5 · icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/skupper-service-controller:8.16.5
```

Depending on which client probes are required, the relevant images need to be available. For example if the VCenter probe is required the following images are required:

- icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/mediation-vcenterbrowsing:8.16.5
- icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic/mediation-vcenter:8.16.5

Note: Unlike the other images, the t8c-client-operator image does not include turbonomic in its path.

When adding these images to a private image registry, the icr.io/cpopen prefix can be removed but the turbonomic prefix must remain.

Following examples show the image registry hosted in docker.acme.com where the images are stored in tsc-images folder. Example image paths are listed:

- docker.acme.com/tsc-images/t8c-client-operator:1.4.1
- docker.acme.com/tsc-images/turbonomic/kube-state-metrics:v2.14.0
- docker.acme.com/tsc-images/turbonomic/tsc-site-resources:8.16.5

```

```

To establish a secure connection between the secure client and the SaaS server, create and apply a token to the secure client. If you have not been provided the URL or login credentials of your SaaS server, contact your Turbonomic representative before proceeding.

1. Create a new token.

Cancel

- a. Log in to your SaaS server.
- b. Click Settings > Secure Client Management .
- c. Select the Client Network Tokens tab and click Create token .
- d. On the Create token dialog, configure the claim limit and the lifespan for the token.

To increase the security of the token, use low values during token creation.

<!-- image -->

Claim limit

Create

x

The claim limit of a token is the number of clients that can be added by using the same token. If you need to connect multiple clients with the same token, increase the claim limit to match the number of clients to be added.

Lifespan

The lifespan of a token is the amount of time before the token expires. An expired token cannot be used to add a client.

An example where the same token can be used for multiple clients is Kubeturbo. If there are many Kubeturbo agents to be connected, it may be convenient to generate one token and apply the same token to each Kubeturbo agent. In this case, increase the claim limit to match the number of Kubeturbo agents to be added and increase the lifespan to allow enough time for the token to be applied to all agents.

- e. Click Create .

Download the token value or copy the token to the clipboard.

2. Apply the token to the secure client.
- a. Open an SSH terminal session on your secure client instance.
- b. Create a file called token.json and add the contents of the token you generated in the UI.
- c. Run the following command in the same namespace that was created before installing the OLM:

```
kubectl apply -f token.json secret/ff108381-e034-11ed-86ed-dee462359331 created
```

CentOS Linux reached end-of-life on June 30, 2024 and is no longer supported. If you are running CentOS Linux 7, migrate to Rocky Linux to continue receiving security updates, fixes, and new features. For more information, see What to know about CentOS Linux EOL.

Starting with version 8.14.1, upgrades to Turbonomic running on CentOS are no longer supported. If you are running CentOS Linux 7, migrate to Rocky Linux to continue receiving security updates, fixes, and new features.

Complete the following steps to migrate the secure client from a CentOS OVA to a Rocky Linux OVA.

1. Open an SSH terminal session to the existing CentOS OVA.
2. Retrieve the existing Turbonomic client custom resource instance. In the example below, turbonomic-client is the namespace in which it is installed.

```
kubectl get tc -n turbonomic-client
```

The output is similar to the following example:

```
NAME                       VERSION turbonomicclient-release   8.16.5
```

3. Determine which probes are currently enabled for the active Turbonomic client instance, which is turbonomicclient-release in this example.

```
kubectl get tc turbonomicclient-release -n turbonomic-client -o yaml | yq '.spec.probes' | grep "enabled: true" -B 1
```

The output is similar to the following example:

```
netApp: enabled: true pure: enabled: true ucs: enabled: true vCenter: enabled: true ...
```

4. Shut down or delete the existing CentOS OVA.
5. Install a new Rocky Linux OVA secure client as described in this topic.
6. Enable any additional probes on the new OVA as described in this topic.
7. Perform the token exchange as described in this topic.

If your environment supports access through a proxy, you can set up the containerd daemon to use that proxy via the HTTP\_PROXY , HTTPS\_PROXY , and NO\_PROXY environment variables.

1. Create the http-proxy.conf file.
2. Configure the proxies in the [Service] section of the file, where NO\_PROXY specifies hosts to exclude from proxying.
3. Reload the daemon and restart containerd.
4. Verify that the HTTP\_PROXY , HTTPS\_PROXY , and NO\_PROXY variables are present in the / etc/ environment file. The NO\_PROXY variable should include the IP of the instance.

```
/etc/systemd/system/containerd.service.d/http-proxy.conf
```

```
[Service] Environment="HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.example.com:80" Environment="HTTPS_PROXY=https://proxy.example.com:443" Environment="NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,containerd-registry.example.com,.corp"
```

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl restart containerd
```

```
cat /etc/environment
```

```
http_proxy=http://PROXY_IP:PROXY_PORT https_proxy=http://PROXY_IP:PROXY_PORT no_proxy=localhost,HOST_IP,node1,127.0.0.1,127.0.0.0,10.233.0.1
```

For more information, see Container runtime changes in Kubernetes 1.24 and beyond on the Kubernetes documentation site.

If none of these options work, you should perform an offline update.

1. Shut down (not power off) the VM for the secure client.
2. Save a snapshot (or clone the VM) of your current secure client. This provides a reliable restore point if you encounter issues during the update. When the snapshot is created, bring the VM back online.
3. Download the ISO image.

```
sudo init 0
```

Refer to the email that you received from IBM for links to the secure client OVA file and ISO image.

4. Save the ISO image to a location that is available to the VM that runs the secure client and then mount the image as a CD drive.

For example, if you run the secure client VM in vCenter server, perform the following steps:

- a. In vCenter, navigate to the secure client VM.
- b. Right-click the VM and choose Edit Settings .
- c. In the CD/DVD Drive dropdown menu, select Datastore ISO , browse to the secure client update ISO image, and then select the image. Verify that Connect at power on is selected.
- d. Open an SSH terminal session to the secure client.
- e. Log in with the System Administrator credentials that you set up when you installed the secure client.
- Username: turbo
- Password: {your\_password}
5. Get the script for your update version.
- a. On your local machine, navigate to the location where the script will be downloaded.
- b. Run the following command as a single line command:

```
curl -O --proxy PROXY_NAME_IP:PORT https://download.vmturbo.com/appliance/download/ updates/ {version} /isoUpdate.sh
```

Where:

- --proxy PROXY\_NAME\_IP:PORT is an optional specification to execute the download through a proxy.
- {version} is the version that you are updating to. The version must be 8.16.5 or later.
6. Upload the script to your secure client instance.

Initiate a file transfer from your local machine to the secure client VM. Save the script to /opt/ local/bin/ directory on the VM that runs the secure client.

7. Make the script executable.
8. Run the offline installation script.

```
chmod +x /opt/local/bin/isoUpdate.sh
```

```
/opt/local/bin/isoUpdate.sh
```

The script performs the following tasks as it runs:

- Mounts the ISO to the directory /mnt/iso/
- Loads the images into the container runtime
- Backs up old scripts
- Updates the deployments to use a private registry where one is configured
- Updates the secure client application
- Unmounts the ISO

After the script updates your platform, wait until all the components start.

kubectl get pods -n turbonomic
```

Kubeturbo can also be deployed without a secure client.

Kubeturbo uses the Turbonomic patented analysis engine to assure the performance of running microservices on Kubernetes or Red Hat OpenShift container platforms.

Deploy Kubeturbo with the secure client to benefit from the following features:

1. Communication from Kubeturbo to the SaaS server uses the existing secure connection established with the secure client.
2. Kubeturbo automatically updates so that it is in sync with the SaaS server version.
3. Logs from Kubeturbo are sent to the SaaS server automatically to keep all historical Kubeturbo logs.

To install Kubeturbo to work with the secure client the following requirements must be met:

1. Deploy Kubeturbo in the same Kubernetes namespace or Red Hat OpenShift project as the secure client.
2. Kubeturbo must be installed using the Kubeturbo Operator.

To deploy to a Kubernetes namespace, use the Kubeturbo operator. For deployment instructions, see this topic.

To deploy to a Red Hat OpenShift project, use OperatorHub. For deployment instructions, see this topic.

Kubeturbo with the secure client is also supported on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) deployments. For more details, see Secure Client Deployment: Other.

The secure client automatically detects Kubeturbo deployments in the same Kubernetes namespace or Red Hat OpenShift project provided that Kubeturbo was installed using the Kubeturbo operator. It then automatically reconfigures the Kubeturbo deployment to use the secure connection provided by the secure client.

Note: If the secure client is running before the Kubeturbo operator is installed, then it might be necessary to restart the secure client operator pod. This is because the secure client operator requires that the Kubeturbo Custom Resource Definition (CRD) exists on the cluster when the secure client operator pod starts. If this is the case, you can restart the secure client operator pod by running the following command:

```
kubectl delete pod t8c-client-operator-controller-manager-<pod-id>
```

If the secure client is removed from the namespace or project, Kubeturbo must be manually reconfigured so that it stops using the secure tunnel connection. Update the turboServer parameter in the Kubeturbo custom resource to point to the Turbonomic instance.

Secure clients that are being used to manage Kubeturbo should not have other probes enabled.

Turbonomic installs as a VM that runs the Rocky Linux 9 OS. For more information about Rocky Linux 9 OS, see https://wiki.rockylinux.org/rocky/version/.

For each new version, Turbonomic delivers a VM image (Open Virtual Appliance (OVA) or Virtual Hard Disk (VHD)) that you install to run the product. Typically, you install this image once, and for subsequent updates to Turbonomic you execute product updates on that installed VM. This means two things:

- Product updates patch new components of the Turbonomic application stack onto the same Rocky platform that you got when you originally installed the VM image. Product updates do not affect the underlying OS.
- Over time, you might learn of important security patches for the Rocky distribution. It is your responsibility to keep the OS up to date. You can install these patches on your Turbonomic VM whenever necessary.

To install the Turbonomic OVA:

1. Download the Turbonomic installation package.

The email you received from IBM includes links to the Turbonomic download pages. You can get the installation package from there.

The installation package includes the turbonomic\_t8c-<version> -<XXXXXXXXXXXXXX> .ova file where <version> is the Turbonomic version number and <XXXXXXXXXXXXXX> is the timestamp.

The OVA file deploys as a VM with the Turbonomic components already installed.

2. Import the OVA file into your datacenter.

Use the vCenter Server client to import the OVA into your environment.

3. Deploy the Turbonomic VM.

Configure the VM that was deployed from the OVA file.

If you want to deploy a VM with 64 GB of memory, manually modify the default value for Memory:

- a. Right-click the VM and select Edit Settings .
- b. Type 64 for Memory.
- c. Click OK to save the settings.
- d. Power on the VM.
4. Open the remote console.

For the Turbonomic VM that you just deployed:

- a. Choose the Summary tab.
- b. Click Launch Remote Console .
5. Set up the Turbonomic System Administrator account.
- a. In the remote console, log in with the following default credentials:
- Username: turbo

Do not use the account name, root .

- Password: vmturbo

Then, you will be prompted to enter a new password.

- b. Enter your new password.

The new password must comply with the strong password policy (a mixture of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and a symbol). Only you will know this new password.

All OVA installs use Kubernetes v1.28.8. Docker commands no longer work. You can use crictl and ctr commands instead. For more information, see the following resources:

- Container runtime changes in Kubernetes 1.28 and beyond on the Kubernetes documentation site
- Mapping from dockercli to crictl on the Kubernetes documentation site
- crictl command reference and information on GitHub

1. Start up the installation script.
- Start a secure session (SSH) on your Turbonomic VM as the turbo user.
- Run the installation script.

/opt/local/bin/t8cInstall.sh

2. Verify that you configured a static IP address for the Turbonomic VM.

After the components start, you will type this static IP address into a web browser to access the login page for the Turbonomic user interface.

As a first step, the script prompts you with:

Have you run the ipsetup script to setup networking yet? [y/n] n

If you did not previously configure a static IP for the platform VM, the setup script will be called on so that you can configure a static IP, and continue the installation.

If you configured a static IP for the platform VM, enter y to continue the installation.

Because of dependencies between Turbonomic and the Kubernetes installation, it is not recommended to change the IP address after the Turbonomic installation. The VM must run with a static IP, regardless if this is a production, testing, or evaluation installation.

If you followed the instructions in OVA: Installing the vCenter Image or in VHD: Installing the vCenter Image, then you already ran the ipsetup script to configure a static IP.

3. Wait while the script completes the installation.

As the installation process continues, the script completes the following installation steps.

- Configures the platform environment with the necessary certificates.
- Configures the Kubernetes cluster on the VM.

Configuring the Kubernetes cluster can take a few tries before it succeeds. For each try that does not succeed, you see messages similar to:

To further debug and diagnose cluster problems, use 'kubectl cluster-info dump'.

When the connection succeeds, the script advances to the next steps.

- Establishes local storage for the platform.
- Creates the Kubernetes namespace for the platform as turbonomic .
- Configures authorization to access the required Kubernetes secrets.
- Initializes the MariaDB database server to manage historical data for the platform.

The script creates two accounts on the MariaDB that have full privileges:

- -root@localhost

This account does not use a password. To connect via this account the user must be system root .

- -mysql@localhost

This account does not use a password. To connect via this account the user must be system mysql .

- Installs the Timescale database for embedded reports and the Data Exporter.
- Deploys and starts up the platform components.

As the deployment begins, the script prints the following:

```
############################ Start the deployment rollout ############################
```

After it deploys the components, it waits for the components to start:

```
The installation process is complete, waiting for all the components to start up.
```

** The script will wait for as long as 30 minutes. **

If the components all start within 30 minutes, then the installation is complete and successful.

If the components do not all start within 30 minutes, the script displays the following and then exits:

```
=========================================================================== One or more of your deployments has not started up yet. ** Please give your environment another 30 minutes to stablize. ** To check the status of your components, execute the following command: kubectl get pods If some components are still not ready, contact your support representative Deployments not ready:
```

The script then displays the formatted result of the kubectl get pods command. This shows you the status of the pods in the Turbonomic platform.

If the script exits before the components all start, give the platform another 30 minutes. To periodically check the component status, run the kubectl get pods command. If the components do not all start after another 30 minutes, contact your support representative.

If the installation is successful and all of the components started, the script displays a message similar to the following, where it gives the VM's static IP address:

```
################################################# Deployment Completed, please login through the UI https://10.10.123.123 #################################################
```

You can move on to the next steps.

4. Save a copy of the platform's Master Key secret.

The installation procedure creates a Master Key secret in the Kubernetes cluster. Turbonomic uses this secret to provide access for the platform components. Save the key data to a safe location.

To save the data:

- a. List the platform secrets.

```
kubectl get secrets
```

The results should include the Master Key secret.

```
... master-key-secret              Opaque                        1      57d ...
```

- b. Display the Master Key data.

After you find the Master Key name, you can then display the key data.

```
kubectl get secret master-key-secret -o yaml
```

The output is similar to the following example:

```
apiVersion: v1 data: primary_key_256.out: AfnJWutxNHAduaIOdAii3DRA2fMa6lzX4rWetZxxZvc= kind: Secret metadata: creationTimestamp: "2021-06-30T02:59:19Z" managedFields: - apiVersion: v1 fieldsType: FieldsV1 fieldsV1: f:data: .: {} f:primary_key_256.out: {} f:type: {} manager: kubectl-create operation: Update time: "2021-06-30T02:59:19Z" name: master-key-secret namespace: turbonomic resourceVersion: "1072" uid: a314b2ba-2061-4b41-b844-56caf2c3728d type: Opaque
```

The important key data to save is the primary\_key... data. In this example, you should save the line:

```
primary_key_256.out: AfnJWutxNHAduaIOdAii3DRA2fMa6lzX4rWetZxxZvc=
```

- c. Save the data to a safe place.

Write this data to a file and save it in a safe backup location. If you ever need to recover the Master Key, your support representative uses this data to perform the recovery.

5. Log in to the Turbonomic user interface using the server address and import your license key.

For more information, see 'Installing license and first-time login' on page 134.

The process that is described here is applicable only to the OVA deployment model.

After you install the Turbonomic VM that will host the platform, you can install the platform components, as follows:

1. (Optional) Configure Single Sign-On Authentication (SSO) for this installation.

If you plan to use SSO to authenticate your Turbonomic users, edit the charts\_v1alpha1\_xl\_cr.yaml file before you complete the installation, or edit it later and restart the affected components. For more information, see Single Sign-On Authentication.

2. Deploy Turbonomic Kubernetes nodes.

When you deploy Turbonomic on Kubernetes, you deploy one Kubernetes node as a VM that hosts pods to run the Turbonomic components. The script to deploy and initialize the Kubernetes node also deploys the Kubernetes pods that make up the Turbonomic application.

Start a secure session (SSH) on your Turbonomic VM as the turbo user and complete the following steps:

- a. Initialize the Kubernetes node and deploy the pods.

```
sudo /opt/local/bin/t8cInstall.sh
```

The script takes up to 20 minutes to complete.

Turbonomic is a containerized microservices platform that installs onto a Kubernetes cluster in a single namespace deployment. The platform uses an operator pattern to deploy, manage, and run the Turbonomic components. The Turbonomic platform operator ( t8c-operator ) uses a Custom Resource Definition (with an Xl kind) and a Custom Resource to configure and adjust your setup.

Currently, installation on Kubernetes clusters is supported on the Red Hat OpenShift platform, AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). It is possible to install on any upstream compliant Kubernetes, but your Turbonomic representative might not be able to provide support.

Before you install Turbonomic, you must configure a remote database server for historical data. This configuration allows for high availability, backups, and handling larger IO demands for larger environments or from remote SQL Server queries. If you are not going to use an existing database server, you must first create a new database server.

For its historical database, Turbonomic supports long-term maintenance stable series of MariaDB (the minimum supported version is 10.6) and MySQL 8.0.x. This support includes comprehensive testing and quality control for Turbonomic usage.

For more information, see Configuring a Remote Database.

This project is used throughout the installation process. The operator must be installed in this project (namespace).

1. Log in to your Red Hat OpenShift console and navigate to Home > Projects .
2. On the Projects page, click Create Project .
3. Specify the project name (for example, turbonomic ).
4. Click Create .
5. Determine the Security Context Constraints (SCC) UID range. This is used later in the install to allow pods to read and write to their PVs.
- a. Open the newly-created project from the Project page and click on the YAML tab.
- b. Find and make note of the Security Context Constraints (SCC) UID range.

You will see a SCC UID value similar to the following example. In this example, 1000680000 is the SCC UID value.

openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range:1000680000/10000

Install Turbonomic into the new project.

1. Navigate to Operators > OperatorHub .
2. In the Filter by keyword box, enter turbonomic to find and select the Turbonomic Platform Operator.

You will see multiple Turbonomic Platform Operator options. To install Turbonomic with a certified operator, ensure you select the "Certified" edition (do not select "Community" or "Marketplace" editions).

3. On the Turbonomic Platform Operator page, read the information about the operator and click Install .
4. On the Install Operator page, specify the Update channel, the project (Namespace) in which you want to install the operator, and the desired Update approval strategy.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to change the repository parameter from the Red Hat Container Catalog to the IBM Container Registry ( icr.io/cpopen ).

```

```

```

The repository parameter must specify icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic as the repository location when working with Red Hat Operators.

3. Specify the external database properties.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to add the properties for the external database you created prior to installation, or remove the parameters to use a containerized database. Do one of the following:

- To use the external database IP address: Update the default externalDbIP value the IP address for your external DB server. If you use a fully qualified domain name for your DB Server, remove this parameter and use externalDBName instead.
- To use the external database name: Replace the externalDbIP parameter with the externalDBName parameter and include the database server's fully qualified domain name (for example, myDBServer.myDomain.com ).
- To use a containerized database: Remove the externalDbIP or externalDBName parameter. If neither are present, a containerized database is created.

Using a containerized database is not supported as it can lead to irrecoverable data corruption. Additionally, a containerized database's performance is directly affected by network performance and cannot be guaranteed. A containerized database should be used for demo, Proof of Concept (POC), or testing purposes only.

The global section shown here is under the parent spec section of the custom resource. This example includes optional parameters and can be used as a guide for MySQL

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: {Edit this value with the IP address for your DB Server. If you use a fully qualified domain name for your DB Server, remove this parameter and use externalDBName instead. If you choose to use a containerized DB, this parameter should be removed} externalDBName: {If not using externalDbIP to specify your DB Server's IP address, use this parameter to specify your DB Server's fully qualified domain name, for example: myDbServer.myDomain.com} properties: global: enableSecureDBConnection: true sqlDialect: MYSQL dbPort: 6033 dbRootPassword: vmturbo dbRootUsername: turboadmin
```

Remove or comment out the sqlDialect parameter when using MariaDB, since MariaDB is the default database server type. Additional properties are required for AWS RDS and Azure DB Services. See documentation for configuring database app users, and provide that information here under properties: global in the parent spec section of the custom resource.

4. Set the Security Context Constraints to allow pods to read and write to their PVs. If this value is not set properly, the pods will not start up successfully.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to include the UID value you noted in step '5' on page 108 in the securityContext: fsGroup: parameter as shown in the following example:

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.5
```

5. Set up Turbonomic to automatically create a Red Hat OpenShift route to the nginx ClusterIP type Service. The Turbonomic operator can create a route for you that functions as the Turbonomic user interface and the endpoint for all remote probes, such as Kubeturbo configured on another cluster.

Edit the Custom Resource YAML to include the nginx as shown in the following example. Change the default nginx from being a primary ingress to function as a proxy, then enable creating a route. The name of the default route that is created is nginx .

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.5 nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false nginxingress: enabled: true openshiftingress: enabled: true
```

(Optional) If you want to manually create your own route to Turbonomic/nginx use only the following parameters:

```
nginx: nginxIsPrimaryIngress: false httpsRedirect: false
```

6. (Optional) If you are working with a private registry, and not the IBM Container Registry, edit the Custom Resource YAML to define registry and repository locations where the default is IBM Container Registry, and make the necessary changes to the operator deployment YAML.

Once the images are in your private registry, edit the repository parameter in the Custom Resource YAML to point to icr.io as the registry location.

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.5
```

If you require credentials to access your registry, you can specify either the image pull secret or the user name and password credentials in the Custom Resource YAML as shown in the following examples.

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 registry: myregistry repository: my.repo/myregistry/turbonomic imagePullSecret: turbocred securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.5
```

```
spec: global: externalDbIP: 10.0.2.15 registry: myregistry repository: my.repo/myregistry/turbonomic imageUsername: turbouser imagePassword: turbopassword securityContext: fsGroup: 1000680000 tag: 8.16.5
```

- The registry parameter is required in the Custom Resource YAML to use the imageUsername/ imagePassword or imagePullSecret parameters.
- This will method creates a Kubernetes secret of type docker-registry with the default name of "turbocred," and then applies the imagePullSecret parameter to the Turbonomic component deployments.
- If using an imagePullSecret , a secret must be created and used instead of the imageUsername and imagePassword . These parameters should only be used when choosing not to utilize an imagePullSecret . See 'Container image repository and pull secrets' on page 44.
7. Click Create to create an instance of the Turbonomic Platform server.
8. When you first install Turbonomic using OperatorHub, target probes are disabled by default. Enable desired target probes, such as IaaS types whether on-prem or cloud.

A probe is a platform component that connects to a target. It discovers the target's entities and loads them into the Turbonomic supply chain, where actions can be executed on entities within the target environment. Turbonomic ships with many probe components that you can use to connect Turbonomic with your environment.

- a. Navigate to Installed Operators > Turbonomic Platform Operator > Turbonomic Platform Operator tab > xl-release .
- b. Edit the Custom Resource YAML to add and enable applicable targets for your instance. For a full description of supported targets, see Target Configuration.

You should not enable Kubeturbo in this step; it should be deployed into the monitored cluster in a separate project (namespace) and configured to communicate with Turbonomic. For more information, see this topic.

All target probes need to be configured in the custom resource using the formatting shown in the following example:

```
spec: global: tag: 8.16.5 ... aws: enabled: true azure: enabled: true dynatrace: enabled: true ...
```

- c. Save and apply your changes to the platform.

1. Navigate to Workloads > Pods to confirm all pods are running and ready, for example 1/1, 2/2, and so on. This may take a few minutes.

If the pods do not run, review the following information for possible solutions:

- Ensure the Security Context Constraints UID is set correctly as noted in the preceding section then restart the pods.
- If you do not have access to the repository that is specified for the container images, check your credentials.
- Ensure the PVs are created and bound to the PVCs.
2. In the Turbonomic project, click Networking > Routes , select the nginx route (or the route you manually created), and click the Location field to open the address of your Turbonomic server (for example, nginx-yourNamespaceName.apps.yourOCPDomain ). This opens a new tab for the Turbonomic user interface.

The operator version that is required by your Turbonomic version is noted in the release notes. The latest version of the operator is 42.84. This version can manage older versions of Turbonomic.

1. Choose from the following options:
- Option 1: Use the default container image repository ( icr.io ) to pull the Turbonomic images.

For this option, download and deploy the operator YAML file. This file specifies icr.io as the repository.

kubectl create -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/t8c-operator/main/deploy/ operator.yaml -n turbonomic

- Option 2: Use a private container image repository to pull the Turbonomic images.

Before proceeding, read the guidelines and instructions for private container image repositories in this topic.

For this option, perform the following steps:

- a. Download the operator YAML file.

wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IBM/t8c-operator/main/deploy/operator.yaml

- b. Open the file for editing (for example, in VS Code or vi ) and then specify your private container image repository in the image parameter.
- c. Deploy the file.

```
image: {your_private_repository}/{directory_path} /t8c-operator:42.84
```

kubectl create -f <location\_of\_downloaded\_YAML\_file> /operator.yaml -n turbonomic

2. Wait for the operator to become ready ( STATUS = Running with READY = 1/1 ).

Run one of the following commands to check the status.

```
kubectl get pods -n turbonomic -w watch kubectl get pods -n turbonomic
```

Complete the following steps to update the CR YAML file ( charts\_v1\_xl\_cr.yaml ) that you downloaded. Since the CR is namespaced, you must be the administrator of your namespace (project) to create an instance of the Turbonomic platform.

When working with YAML files, follow the tips in this topic.

1. Open the YAML file for editing (for example, in VS Code or vi ) . You can use the following command:
2. Update the file with the minimum required parameters:
- Version

```
vi charts_v1_xl_cr.yaml
```

Specify the image tag version.

The image tag version should be in the format x.x.x . This version depends on, and should always match, your Turbonomic instance version. For example, if your Turbonomic instance version is 8.16.5, specify the same instance version as the image tag version.

```
spec: global: tag: <version_to_install>
```

- Database server

If you are installing in a production environment, set up and use a remote database server to take advantage of high availability, backups, and other advanced features. For a test installation in a non-production environment, a containerized database server is sufficient.

- Remote database server

Before proceeding, be sure to configure a remote database server that meets Turbonomic requirements. For more information, see this topic.

When the remote database server is ready, configure the database server parameters using the following examples as guide.

MariaDB configuration example:

```
spec: # Global settings global: repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic tag: 8.16.5 externalDbIP: <MariaDB_host_IP> properties: global: dbRootUsername: <MariaDB_root_username> dbRootPassword: <MariaDB_root_complex_password>
```

MySQL and Azure MySQL configuration example:

```
spec: # Global settings global: repository: icr.io/cpopen/turbonomic tag: 8.16.5 externalDbIP: <MySQL_host_IP> properties: global: sqlDialect: MYSQL enableSecureDBConnection: true dbRootUsername: <MySQL_root_username> dbRootPassword: <MySQL_root_complex_password>
```

Note:

If you want to use the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the remote database server, you need to use the externalDBName parameter.

Remove the externalDbIP parameter from the preceding example and replace it with the externalDBName parameter.

- Containerized database server

To use a containerized database server, remove the externalDbIP parameter.

```
global: externalDbIP:
```
